title: Assistant Site Manager, DashMart - [Nashville, TN]
description:
About the Team
DashMart is a local-fulfillment center owned and operated by DoorDash, offering customers household essentials and other items to their doorsteps with speed, reliability, and quality.
About the Role
In this role, you’ll work within a 5-15k sq ft distribution center, will assist in leading the local warehouse operating team, and in some locations, includes preparing food in a light-prep kitchen, and help the Site Manager ensure we maintain high quality for our customers.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Lead: You’ll demonstrate compassion and commitment to inclusivity as you lead a team of hourly Operations Associates and Shift Leads. You’ll hire, coach and develop high-performing team members, while building a safety-first culture where employees are excited to drive success, personally and for the team. You’ll serve as a leading change agent for your site, helping your team to navigate new initiatives and growth projects. You’ll tackle onsite escalations, including coordination with cross-functional partners.
Operate: With your thumb on the pulse of all outcomes for your team, you will be directly responsible for driving results in one or more specific focus areas or a specific shift for your site. To achieve your performance targets, you’ll drive success through effective scheduling and by executing inventory management processes and deploying best practices from across the network. You’ll engage cross-functional partners as needed for support.
Strategize: Within the focus area(s) assigned by your Site Manager, you’ll analyze data and make strategic recommendations and execute actions regarding resource allocation, workflow, warehouse organization and when to engage cross-functional partners. You may also lead some process improvement projects.
Delight: We are customer-obsessed. You’ll coach and empower your team to provide a highly quality customer experience with every order. Quality metrics such as order accuracy and fulfillment speed will be key measurements of success for your team. You’ll also work cross-functionally with central teams from our inventory to training teams to ensure your team has the tools and resources they’ll need to deliver.
We’re excited about you because…
You’re a proven leader. You have managed high-performance teams of 5+ employees with successful performance and employee development outcomes.
You relish ownership. You’re excited to have ownership in a new and rapidly growing business. No problem is too big or too small for you, and you’re ready to show up however needed for your team.
You solve problems from first principles.   You’re excited to solve problems in innovative ways, and you resist “this is how it’s always been done” thinking.
You’re unafraid of ambiguity.   Rapid change and learning is exciting to you, and you thrive in ambiguous, startup environments.
You’re analytical . You let data win arguments. You are a data-first problem solver and you have experience using Excel or Google Sheets to analyze data, including using basic formulas and creating pivot tables.
You have 3+ years’ experience : In Operations, Warehouse Logistics, Customer Service, Retail Management, Fulfillment, or related field
You have 1+ years of experience managing a team
You have flexibility in your schedule. As the leader of the site, you will need to ensure your team and the site is fully supported, which will include regularly scheduled late-night and weekend hours.
About DoorDash
At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods.
DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees’ happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more.
Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion
We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

title: Associate, Strategy & Operations, Merchant Onboarding & Experience
description:
About the Team
The New Vertical Onboarding Strategy & Operations team drives a fast, seamless onboarding experience for merchants across the SMB segments. We collaborate closely with cross-functional partners to enhance visibility, streamline workflows, and reduce onboarding friction through scalable process and product improvements. Our mission is to ensure every merchant launches smoothly and efficiently, powered by data-driven insights and strong operational alignment.
About the Role
The SMB Onboarding Strategy & Operations (S&O) role focuses on improving the end-to-end onboarding experience for small and medium-sized merchants by identifying process inefficiencies, building visibility tools, and driving scalable solutions across cross-functional teams. This role acts as the single-threaded owner for SMB onboarding, ensuring merchants are launched quickly, accurately, and with minimal friction through data-driven insights, process automation, and clear ownership alignment.
Key Responsibilities
Process Visibility & SLA Tracking: Build dashboards to monitor true onboarding timelines, identify delays, and surface insights to inform process and tooling improvements.
Root Causing Blocked Cases: Develop a shared tracker for blocked cases, analyze trends, and work with cross-functional partners to resolve issues and implement sustainable fixes.
Integrations Enablement: Design and refine onboarding workflows for new integration types (e.g., Shopify), and establish scalable processes as SMB Retail expands in 2026.
Product & Tooling Guidance: Translate workflow gaps into actionable product requirements for systems like SFDC, and advocate for automation that reduces manual work.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with MXO, GTMT, IA, Sales, and Product to ensure end-to-end alignment on onboarding priorities and execution.
Data & Insights: Create and maintain onboarding performance dashboards to measure success and track progress toward SLAs and OKRs.
You will report into the Manager of the Onboarding S&O pod on our Merchant Onboarding & Experience S&O team in our New Verticals Business Development organization.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Drive meaningful impact by transforming how SMB merchants onboard — reducing friction, accelerating launch timelines, and improving the overall merchant experience.
Shape strategy and process from the ground up, building visibility tools, performance metrics, and scalable workflows that become the foundation for SMB onboarding excellence.
Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Sales, Ops, and GTMT to design solutions that balance speed, quality, and automation across the onboarding journey.
Own high-visibility problem areas, using data to identify blockers and lead systemic, cross-team improvements that directly impact business growth.
Be at the forefront of innovation, helping define the future of merchant onboarding as new integrations, verticals, and tooling capabilities are unlocked in 2026 and beyond
We’re excited about you because…
You have 2+ years of experience in a fast-paced environment, where you’ve built and optimized processes from the ground up.
You’re proficient in SQL and comfortable using data to uncover insights, measure impact, and inform operational or strategic decisions.
You thrive in dynamic, fast-moving environments, adapting quickly while maintaining a high bar for execution and detail.
You’re a strong cross-functional collaborator.
You’re known for your ability to “herd cats” — driving accountability, clarifying ownership, and keeping complex projects on track amid competing priorities.
You possess a strategic and analytical mindset, able to diagnose root causes and translate findings into actionable, scalable solutions.
You have exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills, capable of influencing without authority across seniority levels and functions.
You’re systems- and process-oriented, with a knack for identifying inefficiencies and translating workflow pain points into clear product or tooling requirements.
You’re impact-driven, motivated by improving merchant experiences and accelerating business outcomes through operational excellence.
You’re energized by ambiguity, eager to define structure, build visibility, and create sustainable frameworks that set the foundation for long-term success.
We expect this position to be filled by 10-17-2026
Compensation
Actual compensation within the pay range listed below will be decided based on factors including, but not limited to, skills, prior relevant experience, and specific work location. Base salary is localized according to employee work location.
DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others.
To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here .

For salaried roles: flexible paid time off/vacation, plus 80 hours of paid sick time per year.

title: Electrical Engineer - Consumer Electronics
description:
About the Team
DoorDash Labs, established in 2018, serves as the innovation hub for DoorDash, focusing on developing automation and robotics solutions to enhance last-mile logistics. The team's mission is to create technologies that support and augment human networks, aiming to improve efficiency for Dashers, merchants, and consumers alike.  We’re ruthlessly focused on business impact.  We are a highly senior team composed of former pioneers from a variety of different robotics industries.  As of 2025, DoorDash has completed 10B lifetime deliveries.  We’re focused on how to do the next 10B even better.
About the Role
We’re looking for a Senior/Staff electrical and firmware engineer who designs the board and writes the firmware for connected consumer and enterprise devices, including tablets, POS systems, peripherals, and emerging robotics applications.
In this role, you will take connected devices from ambiguous user or business needs through system architecture, rapid prototyping, board design, firmware implementation, bring-up, field deployment, and production transition.
The ideal candidate has a passion for building and shipping reliable hardware at scale and thrives in an environment that demands technical depth and high-quality execution across multiple concurrent programs. This is a build-heavy role on a small, senior team.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Own connected devices end to end, including:
Own connected devices from an ambiguous product need through field deployment.
Work across the hardware and firmware boundary instead of handing work between specialists.
Explore uncertain product ideas through rapid prototypes and experiments.
Make consequential tradeoffs on a small, senior team with direct exposure to users and field behavior.
Key Responsibilities
Translate user and business needs into an integrated electrical and firmware architecture.
Design compute-based, mixed-signal boards incorporating processors, power systems, sensors, wireless connectivity, displays, and other peripherals.
Develop embedded firmware, selecting bare metal, FreeRTOS, embedded Linux, or Android based on product needs.
Lead board bring-up, validation, and troubleshooting using lab tools (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, spectrum analyzers, network analyzers, etc.).
Prototype with new sensors and run experiments to determine whether useful, reliable signals can be extracted.
Own the full lifecycle of electrical hardware from concept, schematic capture, layout review, through bring-up, validation, certification, and production handoff.
Collaborate with mechanical, software, product, and operations partners while making tradeoffs among speed, reliability, cost, manufacturability, and user experience.
Contribute across multiple programs — including merchant-facing hardware and emerging automation or robotics efforts — as business needs evolve.
We're excited about you because...
Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field.
8+ years of hands-on product-development experience spanning electrical hardware and embedded firmware.
You have taken customer-facing or field-deployed hardware from early concept through production, with experience scaling designs beyond initial deployments.
You have personally designed a board and written its production firmware on the same product. This is the core requirement: genuine dual capability, not adjacency to it.
You have hands-on depth in compute-based board design, embedded C/C++, board bring-up, and hardware debugging.
You can independently develop a system architecture from incomplete requirements.
You have sufficient experience across power, wireless, sensors, and interfaces to lead the whole electrical system.
Must be comfortable regularly exercising discretion and independent judgment in performing job duties, including evaluating options, making informed decisions, and determining appropriate courses of action within the scope of assigned responsibilities.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience developing tablets, POS systems, or other connected consumer/enterprise devices.
Experience with regulatory compliance and certification processes (FCC, CE, etc.).
Exposure to electromechanical or robotics systems.
You’ve shipped hardware at scale in customer-facing products.
You are an engineer in your personal life and have the projects to prove it.
Have worked with in-house and contract manufacturing teams.
Thrive in high-integrity, fast-paced, high-ownership environments and care deeply about craftsmanship.
Live and breathe extreme ownership.

The DoorDash Air team is bringing drone delivery to reality. To make this happen, we’re building a strong electrical team to design high reliability, high power density converters, and fault-tolerant controls electronics. Come join us to build a new class of aircrafts and deploy at scale.
DoorDash Labs, established in 2018, serves as the innovation hub for DoorDash, focusing on developing automation and robotics solutions to enhance last-mile logistics. The team's mission is to create technologies that support and augment human networks, aiming to improve efficiency for Dashers, merchants, and consumers alike.  We’re ruthlessly focused on business impact.  We are a highly senior team composed of former pioneers from a variety of different robotics industries.  As of 2025, DoorDash has completed 10B lifetime deliveries.  We’re focused on how to do the next 10B even better.
About the Role
As the Product Manager Airspace & Autonomy for DoorDash Air’s Airspace and Autonomy capabilities, you will own the end-to-end product strategy for the software, services, autonomy, perception, human interfaces and related capabilities required to deploy autonomous drone delivery at scale.
You will connect DoorDash’s order and logistics platform with the aircraft, autonomy stack, mission-planning services, UTM capabilities, fleet-management tools, and operator workflows that execute each delivery. You will define how an order moves from merchant readiness through dispatch, airspace validation, autonomous flight, delivery, and completion within the broader DoorDash marketplace, ensuring that new features align to DoorDash Air’s roadmap across teams while balancing execution timelines against technical debt.
You will lead product direction across autonomy, aviation software, services, hardware, systems engineering, flight operations, UTM, safety, regulatory, data, and DoorDash platform teams. You will work closely with the Head of UTM and senior Engineering and Operations leaders to establish the product roadmap, clarify system boundaries, make build-versus-partner decisions, and align technical investment with operational scale and unit economics. You will also coach and mentor engineers to help them understand how their work contributes to the broader vision and enables safe and scalable drone delivery operations.
This is not a coordination-only role, nor is it purely an internally facing role. You will already have deep credibility in standards development organizations and will promote best practices to help ensure that DoorDash Air’s software, services and hardware meet technical standards required for regulatory compliance in the U.S. and abroad. You will set the vision, establish priorities, make informed technical and product tradeoffs, and hold cross-functional teams accountable for delivering an integrated drone delivery system.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Own the end-to-end product strategy for DoorDash Air’s safety critical software, services and platform infrastructure. Define the long-term vision, platform architecture, capability roadmap, and investment priorities across aircraft, onboard software, cloud services, operational tooling, and DoorDash platform integrations.
Integrate drone delivery into the DoorDash marketplace. Define how merchant preparation, order readiness, dispatch timing, routing, customer promises, delivery-zone eligibility, and fulfillment decisions interact with aircraft availability, weather, airspace, and operational constraints.
Lead the autonomy product roadmap. Establish priorities across mission planning, autonomous path and motion planning, contingency behaviors, rerouting, detect-and-avoid integration, vehicle health, payload handling, landing and delivery behaviors, and remote assistance.
Create the roadmap to progress from 1:1 to m:N operations. Define the incremental technical capabilities required to move from one operator supervising one aircraft toward increasingly autonomous multi-aircraft operations, including exception management, alert prioritization, task allocation, fleet orchestration, remote intervention, and human-autonomy interface design.
Define the data strategy for autonomous aviation. Determine which geospatial, terrain, obstacle, weather, airspace, population-risk, connectivity, landing-zone, and operational data layers should be built internally, licensed, sourced through partners, or generated by the fleet.
Build UTM and airspace-management capabilities. Lead product requirements for operational-volume generation, strategic and tactical deconfliction, dynamic rerouting, airspace authorization, constraint management, conformance monitoring, and interoperability with UTM service providers and public airspace systems.
Lead standards compliance and engagement. Champion compliance with relevant standards — ASTM F3201 (software), F3548 and F3411 (UTM-specific functions) — across the airspace software roadmap and specs. Maintain an active leadership role in ASTM standards-development activities on behalf of DoorDash.
Productize regulatory compliance. Translate Part 135 operating requirements, BVLOS approvals, safety cases, operational limitations, and emerging Part 108 concepts into reusable software, data, workflow, auditability, and configuration-management capabilities.
Make build, buy, and partner decisions. Evaluate technology providers, data sources, autonomy components, and infrastructure partners based on strategic differentiation, integration complexity, operational risk, economics, and time to market.
Define system-level success metrics. Work across the organization to establish instrumentation and KPIs across delivery success, order-to-dispatch time, route efficiency, intervention frequency, operator-to-aircraft ratio, aircraft utilization, mission completion, system availability, regulatory conformance, and cost per delivery.
Connect technical investment to business outcomes. Develop business cases and sequencing recommendations that balance safety, customer experience, operational scalability, engineering effort, deployment speed, and long-term unit economics.
Shape the technical organization. Identify the product, systems, autonomy, platform, data, hardware, test, and operational capabilities required to achieve the roadmap. Partner with functional leaders to define roles, close talent gaps, and build an organization capable of scaling beyond individual experts.
We’re excited about you because…
10+ years of product management, technical product leadership, systems leadership, or related experience, including significant responsibility for complex software or cyber-physical platforms.
5+ years of experience in autonomous systems, robotics, UAS, aviation technology, safety-critical systems, or another highly regulated real-world operating environment.
A demonstrated track record of taking technically complex products from early concept or prototype through validation, deployment, and operational scale.
Experience owning products that span multiple layers of a technology stack, including embedded or vehicle software, cloud services, APIs, data infrastructure, operational applications, and hardware integration.
Strong technical fluency across autonomous-system concepts such as mission planning, path planning, motion planning, perception, localization, guidance and control, behavior management, contingency handling, simulation, telemetry, and command and control.
Experience defining product strategy and architecture for distributed, real-time, or mission-critical systems in which reliability, safety, and operational performance are fundamental product requirements.
Working knowledge of UTM, airspace-management systems, geospatial data, flight-planning services, operational volumes, conformance monitoring, and airspace interoperability.
Experience operating within or building technology for FAA-regulated environments, including familiarity with any combination of National Airspace System hardware/software/procedures, Part 107, Part 135, Part 108, Part 146, BVLOS operating approvals, UTM or USS services, and evolving autonomous-flight regulations.
Experience designing or scaling human-supervised autonomy, remote operations, multi-vehicle systems, fleet orchestration, or m:N operating models.

description:
About the Team
DoorDash's MDX team sits within Machine Learning Platform and builds the shared foundation that ML engineers across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo rely on to build and run ML-powered products. We work across the full ML lifecycle: feature engineering, training, evaluation, deployment, serving, and monitoring. Our mission is to increase the velocity and reliability of ML-driven business impact across the company. A central pillar of that work is agentic infrastructure. We are building systems that let agents accelerate and operate the ML workflow itself, including auto research, where agents explore and iterate on modeling ideas, and self-healing systems that detect, diagnose, and remediate failures in ML pipelines and production models with minimal human intervention.
About the Role
You will join a small, high-leverage team building the agentic layer of DoorDash's ML infrastructure. You'll design and build the systems that let agents accelerate how ML engineers across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo develop, ship, and operate models. That includes auto research systems that explore and iterate on modeling ideas, and agentic developer support that helps ML engineers move through training, evaluation, deployment, and debugging faster. You'll own well-scoped components end to end, from design through production, working across agent orchestration, tooling and integrations with our ML platform, evaluation of agent behavior, and observability. This role is ideal for an engineer with a strong backend foundation who is excited to apply AI agents to real engineering workflows, learns quickly, and wants to grow into technical leadership in a fast-moving area where model capabilities, tooling, and best practices change month to month.
You're excited about this opportunity because you will…
Build agentic systems that increase the velocity of ML development across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo, helping ML engineers get from idea to production model faster.
Design and implement infrastructure that lets agents propose, run, and evaluate modeling experiments.
Build agentic developer support for the ML lifecycle, such as agents that help engineers set up training jobs, debug failing pipelines, review model deployments, and navigate our platform.
Develop evaluation and observability for agent behavior, so we can measure whether agents are actually helping, catch regressions early, and build the trust needed to give them more autonomy.
Work with production standards in mind, including reliability, safety guardrails, cost controls, monitoring, and clear playbooks, so that agentic workflows can run against real ML systems.
Partner closely with ML engineers, data scientists, and platform teams to understand where their time goes and turn those workflows into durable, reusable platform capabilities.
Grow quickly in a fast-moving area, with the chance to shape how agents are used to build and operate ML systems at a company of this scale.

B.S., M.S., or PhD in Computer Science or equivalent

title: Staff Software Engineer, Data - Experimentation
location: California, CA; San Francisco, CA; Seattle, WA; New York,NY
description:
About the Team
The Decision Systems team helps DoorDash teams make faster, more rigorous, and more trustworthy decisions. We build the analytical systems, statistical methods, and product experiences that power experimentation, causal inference, rollout analysis, metric interpretation, and business impact measurement across DoorDash’s three-sided marketplace. Curie is DoorDash’s experiment analysis product within Decision Systems. It sits at the center of how teams move from hypothesis to analysis to confident action, helping decision makers understand experiments, rollouts, metric movements, and marketplace impact while preserving scientific rigor, velocity, trust, and interpretability. Our work spans experimentation platforms, causal inference, variance reduction, switchback experimentation, metric systems, and AI-assisted analysis workflows. We partner closely with data scientists, engineers, product managers, and operators across DoorDash to translate advanced methods into reliable, scalable systems that improve decision quality and product velocity. Some of the work done in the team was published in articles such as: Design-Aware Variance Reduction for Switchback Experiments: A Comparative Study , Power-Optimal Covariate Adjustment for Switchback Experiments , CUPED on Steroids: Multivariate Covariate Adjustment for Switchback Experiments .
About the Role
We are looking for a Staff Applied Scientist to provide scientific leadership for DoorDash’s Experimentation Platform. In this role, you will define and advance the statistical, causal inference, machine learning, and AI capabilities that power high-quality decision-making across DoorDash. You will work on challenging problems at the intersection of experimentation, marketplace dynamics, machine learning, and product engineering.
Your work will shape how DoorDash teams design experiments, analyze results, interpret noisy marketplace outcomes, and make faster, more trustworthy decisions. This is a high-leverage role for a scientist who enjoys both deep technical work and broad cross-functional influence—partnering with engineers, data scientists, product managers, and operators to translate cutting-edge methods into reliable platform capabilities used across the company.
You're excited about this opportunity because you will...
Set the scientific direction for Curie and shape the Decision Systems roadmap with engineering and product partners, identifying where better science, tooling, or automation can materially improve decision quality and velocity.
Own the statistical contract for experiment analysis, including how metrics, populations, exposure windows, covariates, ratio metrics, and edge cases are defined.
Ensure production systems faithfully implement those contracts by reviewing analytical SQL, validating statistical parity, and raising the bar for correctness across engine migrations.
Develop and productionize advanced methods such as CUPED/CUPAC, ratio-metric and delta-method inference, sequential testing, heterogeneous treatment effects, switchback designs, and difference-in-differences for marketplace interference.
Build approaches that hold up in high-scale, high-noise, three-sided marketplace data, including power analysis, multiple-testing correction, winsorization, quantile metrics, and other robust measurement techniques.
Advance AI-assisted analysis workflows, including trustworthy automated experiment readouts, risk detection, and hypothesis generation, with the same rigor expected of statistical methods.
Advise and mentor data scientists, product teams, operators, and engineers on experimental design, metric strategy, causal analysis, and interpretation of results.
We're excited about you because you have…
6+ years of industry experience, or equivalent applied research experience, developing statistical, causal inference, machine learning, or experimentation systems with measurable business impact.
Deep expertise in experimentation and causal inference, with production experience in methods such as variance reduction, ratio metrics, sequential testing, heterogeneous treatment effects, marketplace interference, or quasi-experimental designs.
Strong coding and data skills, including the ability to reason about production data pipelines and review complex analytical SQL for statistical correctness.
Experience translating statistical or machine learning methods into reliable, scalable platform capabilities in close partnership with engineering and product teams.
A track record of setting technical direction, influencing cross-functional teams, and mentoring senior technical contributors without relying solely on formal authority.
The ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to scientific, engineering, product, and executive audiences.
A bias for impact: you know how to balance methodological rigor, product velocity, engineering constraints, and customer needs.

As a Mechanical Engineer I, you will play a critical role in turning electrode and battery concepts into physical test vehicles, from standard platforms to custom builds for novel experiments. You will take designs from CAD through fabrication and assembly, and then put working hardware in the hands of the scientists and engineers who use it to accelerate discovery and development. Your work will help us build and validate a complex, novel product that supports a more reliable electric grid. This is an exciting opportunity to help shape and be part of the growth of a fast-moving company with breakthrough technology and an incredible mission! Relocation assistance is available. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Design standard and custom test vehicles, balancing performance, manufacturability, and speed to test

 - Fabricate prototypes and proofs of concept, iterating quickly based on build and test feedback

 - Work with technicians to streamline builds and improve the reliability and repeatability of assembly

 - Partner with scientists and engineers to design tools and fixtures that expand our discovery and development capabilities

 - Produce CAD models and engineering drawings that technicians, machinists, and vendors can build from, and release them through our documentation process

 - Manage multiple projects at once and adjust as priorities shift

 - Follow lab and shop safety practices and design hardware for safe operation




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field

 - 0-2 years of experience in mechanical design, through industry roles, internships, co-ops, or research and project work

 - Proficiency in 3D CAD and 2D drafting using SolidWorks or a similar tool, including familiarity with GD&T fundamentals

 - Hands-on aptitude for prototyping, with experience in fabrication methods such as machining, 3D printing, or sheet metal

 - Ability to write clear technical documentation, including work instructions that others can follow

 - Strong communication and collaboration skills, with comfort working alongside scientists, engineers, and technicians

 - Intellectual curiosity, a pragmatic approach to problem-solving, and a willingness to learn quickly

 - Comfort with complexity and a commitment to safety, quality, and the people you work with

Google's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. Our products need to handle information at massive scale, and extend well beyond web search. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. As a software engineer, you will work on a specific project critical to Google’s needs with opportunities to switch teams and projects as you and our fast-paced business grow and evolve. We need our engineers to be versatile, display leadership qualities and be enthusiastic to take on new problems across the full-stack as we continue to push technology forward.
Our engineering domain spans the full networking and security stack from enforcing continuous identity and device posture checks on every request, to architecting customer-dedicated egress routing, seamless GCP VPC integration, and multi-cloud connectivity. Because we operate in the critical path of enterprise productivity, our systems are engineered for extreme resiliency, deep observability, and the highest regulatory compliance standards (FedRAMP, DoD IL5, HIPAA, etc.), all without adding perceptible latency to the end-user browsing experience.
Application Instructions: In most instances, this position requires in-person interviews as part of the hiring process.
Chrome is dedicated to building a better, more open web. We’re focused on making a better browser (on both desktop and mobile) to help users take advantage of all the web has to offer in a safe and secure way.Chrome is available across all major platforms — iOS, Android, Windows, Mac, Linux and Chrome OS. We also built Chrome as an open source project so the entire web ecosystem could benefit from the latest innovations in speed, simplicity and security.

You will join a dynamic and diverse team in a professional office setting. This role requires the ability to travel up to 15–20% domestically, ranging from day trips to week-long excursions depending on the product lifecycle.

At ITW, we offer a professional environment where your decisions directly affect the financial success of the product line. title: Inventory Control Coordinator
description:
Job Description:
Why this Role Matters
The Inventory Control Coordinator at ITW in Paris, Kentucky plays a critical role in ensuring manufacturing operations have the tooling, materials, and non-inventory supplies needed to meet customer demand. You will leverage analytical thinking and 80/20 principles to optimize inventory levels, improve material availability, reduce stock-outs and excess inventory, and strengthen supplier performance. Success in this role means maintaining a reliable supply chain that supports operational efficiency, cost control, and continuous improvement.
What You Will Do
Analyze inventory levels and consumption patterns to ensure on-hand materials meet manufacturing requirements, including expedited and exceptional production needs as communicated.
Support root cause analysis initiatives by evaluating reports, identifying usage trends, monitoring consumption changes, and investigating unusual inventory patterns.
Manage the RFQ process for all non-inventory materials, tooling, and related supplies.
Place purchase orders and proactively follow up on open orders while ensuring compliance with established pricing, discounts, and purchasing terms.

title: Senior Product Manager
description:
Job Description:
Senior Product Manager – Warewash Division – Troy, OH
Illinois Tool Works (ITW) is a Fortune 200 company that produces diversified products in global markets.  Some of its products include welding equipment, automotive components, construction materials and commercial food equipment.  The Food Equipment Group is one of seven ITW decentralized business segments.  The Warewash Division is seeking a Senior Product Manager (in office) at its Troy, Ohio facility, located 20 minutes north of the Dayton metropolitan area.
The Warewash Business Division produces Hobart, Stero and Somat branded commercial dishwashers, waste equipment and disposers used in hotels, retail, restaurants, cruise ships, schools, universities, and other environments.  We are the industry leader and seeking to expand our growth in existing served markets as well as new markets.  We are in search of a Senior Product Manager to help support and grow the FEG Warewash business through market research, product development, go-to-market planning, demand generation, and sales and channel support for our commercial line of dishwashers.  This position champions the voice of the customer with engineering and product development teams and provides support to our sales development managers and field sales organization to maximize sales volume for the business unit’s products.
Summary:
The Senior Product Manager will identify new market opportunities, develop market strategies, manage the product portfolio, develop marketing plans for new and existing products, define product training requirements, and develop programs to ensure the field sales organization and dealer and consultant communities have accurate product knowledge and a clear sales narrative to drive success with the Hobart line.
We are seeking candidates with demonstrated success defining product and portfolio strategy, leading complex cross-functional initiatives, making strategic recommendations, and delivering measurable business results. Relevant experience includes market and competitive analysis, strategic leadership, product development and lifecycle management, major product launches, go-to-market planning, and sales and service enablement.
What you will do:
Product Development & Management
Own and define the mid-to-long-term strategy, product vision, and roadmap for a major product line and contribute to strategic direction across the Warewash portfolio.
Lead ongoing discovery of new product and business opportunities through competitor and market analysis and primary and secondary customer research using ITW’s Market-Segment-Focus approach.
Work collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders to translate market segment insights, customer needs, competitive dynamics, and financial considerations into product specifications, business cases, value propositions, and product roadmaps for the U.S. commercial dishwashing market.
Lead cross-functional New Product Development teams ensuring alignment with North American commercial dishwashing customer needs and pain points through clear product specifications, business plans and product launches for each product line.
Support for Business Development & Product Line Growth
Drive organic revenue growth and market share expansion goals through commercialization, demand generation, strategic product positioning, customer engagement, and sales enablement activities.
Develop and execute go-to-market and commercial launch plans for new product launches ensuring alignment across sales, service, operations, channel partners, and marketing.
Provide customized marketing, product specification, research, and other direct support to sales teams for key account opportunities.
Develop and deliver product sales training and support to field teams, dealers, consultants, and service partners through product presentations, product marketing collateral and in-the-field training.
Provide continuous updates to competitive and market intelligence and customer trends that affect success in targeted accounts and segments.
Define and communicate the product vision and value proposition for assigned product lines, leveraging customer insights, competitive intelligence, market trends, and product performance data to align stakeholders around growth opportunities and guide strategic decision-making.
Leadership
Provide strategic leadership and project management for sales, marketing, engineering, and other functions for effective product development and product launches.
Spend time in key segments and channels with team members and customers to understand market needs and provide training on Hobart WW products and sales narratives.
Mentor and coach Product Managers and cross-functional team members, strengthening product-management practices, strategic thinking, and execution discipline.
What we are looking for:
Advanced knowledge of product marketing concepts and strategies
Demonstrated ability to own product or portfolio strategy, establish a mid-to-long-term roadmap, and connect priorities to revenue, profitability, market-share, and customer-value outcomes
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex market, customer, and business data to identify trends, develop strategic recommendations, and drive business decisions
Extensive experience interacting with and presenting to customers and a variety of business stakeholders
Proven expertise in leading primary and secondary market research initiatives and translating customer, market, and competitive insights into product vision, product and portfolio strategies, product roadmaps, and technical requirements
Proven success leading complex cross-functional initiatives through influence and aligning senior or executive stakeholders around product and portfolio choices
Experience mentoring or coaching Product Managers or other cross-functional professionals
Excellent verbal, written, interpersonal communications as well as effective presentation skills
Proficiency in MS Office applications
Ability to travel 10% - 15%
Education and experience:
Required:
Bachelor’s Degree
7+ years of experience in a relevant role with demonstrated results
2 or more significant product launch cycles
Proven experience utilizing engineering stage-gate and new product development processes to successfully lead products from concept development through launch and lifecycle management
Preferred:
Preference for a degree majoring in Marketing, Business, or Engineering
Commercial kitchen equipment knowledge
2+ years of food service industry experience
Take this opportunity to join a successful and enthusiastic global team where we value the inclusion of diverse team members.  You will enjoy a competitive salary and generous benefits that includes health, dental, life and STD/LTD insurance, 401k (with match), and an education tuition reimbursement program.

title: Site and Service Manager
description:
Job Description:
Position Summary
The Site & Service Manager is responsible for overall growth, performance, and strategic direction of the company’s rental and repair operations across multiple locations. This role provides leadership and oversight for the department, to ensure long term operational efficiency, scalability, and organizational effectiveness. Working collaboratively with department leadership and cross-functional teams, the position assesses operational processes, staffing structures, and business opportunities to support continued growth and improvement. The Site & Service Manager is accountable for ensuring the rental and repair operation is structured and positioned to meet current and future business objectives.
Core Responsibilities:
Provide strategic leadership and oversight of site, rental, repair, warehouse, and facility operations across multiple locations to ensure operational excellence and achievement of business objectives.
Partner with department leadership to monitor performance, resolve operational challenges, and maintain efficient day to day operations while supporting business continuity.
Develop, implement, and standardize processes, procedures, and operational standards that improve efficiency, service quality, consistency, and turnaround times.
Evaluate organizational structure, staffing, workflows, and resource allocation to ensure scalability, productivity, and alignment with current and future business needs.
Lead the planning, launch, and ongoing performance management of new warehouse and service locations, including operational readiness and facility oversight.
Establish and manage relationships with vendors, contractors, landlords, and service partners, including contract negotiations, to support operational effectiveness, and strategic growth.
Analyze KPIs and operational data to drive continuous improvement, profitability, customer satisfaction, cost efficiencies, and business growth while providing recommendations and reporting leadership.
Oversee purchasing activities, vendor relationships, purchase orders and timely procurement of materials, supplies, and equipment.
Apply ITW’s 80/20 principles to inventory planning and replenishment activities, maintaining target product availability levels that support customer, sales, rental, and service requirements.
Manage inventory investment and working capital by achieving Months on Hand (MOH) targets while balancing customer service, availability, and operational efficiency.
Drive inventory health through proactive management of slow-moving and obsolete inventory, simplifying inventory complexity and optimizing stock levels.
Partner with suppliers, warehouse operations, logistics providers, rental facilities, and cross-functional teams to improve product availability, delivery performance, inventory flow, and overall customer experience.
Continuously identify and eliminate nonvalue added activities, simplify processes, and implement improvements that enhance supply chain responsiveness, efficiency, and customer outcomes.
Growth Mindset – Embraces learning, feedback, and continuous improvement
Entrepreneurial Spirit – Takes initiative, identifies opportunities, and approaches challenges with a proactive, solutions-oriented mindset.
Ownership & Collaboration – Takes accountability for results while working effectively with others to achieve shared goals.
Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Business, Operations Management, Supply Chain Management, Engineering, or a related field preferred.
7+ years of progressive leadership experience in operations, equipment rental, service, manufacturing, distribution, or a related industrial environment.
Demonstrated success leading multi-site operations, managing geographically dispersed teams, and supporting organizational growth.
Experience developing, launching and managing new facilities, warehouses, or operational locations.
Strong knowledge of equipment rental operations, repair, and maintenance practices, inventory management, customer service, and workplace safety regulations (including OSHA requirements).
Proven ability to analyze operational and financial performance metrics, negotiate contracts, manage vendor relationships, and utilize ERP systems, rental management software, Microsoft Office, and reporting tools to drive business results.
Growth Mindset – Embraces learning, feedback, and continuous improvement
Entrepreneurial Spirit – Takes initiative, identifies opportunities, and approaches challenges with a proactive, solutions – oriented mindset.
Ownership & Collaboration – Takes accountability for results while working effectively with others to achieve shared goals.

Lean Manufacturing or Lean Operations experience.
Six Sigma Green Belt or equivalent continuous improvement training.
Experience with KPI development and performance management.
Experience in the welding, industrial equipment, construction equipment or related industries preferred.
Travel: Must be willing and able to travel about 20%

Comprehensive training on company products and sales strategies.
Opportunities for professional development and career growth.

title: Videographer & Motion Editor
description:
Job Description:
Job Summary
This is a high-impact, technical role for a video and motion professional who takes pride in the craft of visual storytelling. You will be a driving force for ITW Welding's family of brands, primarily Miller and Hobart, turning brand strategies and creative briefs into authentic, genuine video content that honors our nearly 100-year legacy. You will bridge the gap between the gritty reality of the shop floor and the high-stakes precision of the corporate boardroom. You will be responsible for capturing our distinct brand voices with the same honesty found in the work itself, creating content that speaks with equal authority to the welding fabricator at the bench, the leaders in the boardroom, and the distribution partners who rely on our brand reputation to drive their sales. You are a "master of the craft" and hands-on creative partner who advises and influences the vision while executing the work with technical precision.
Responsibilities
Cinematic Execution & Technical Strategy
Serve as a primary cinematographer on set, managing composition, lighting, and sound while providing technical video expertise alongside our product experts to capture the authentic reality of the work.
Utilize our dedicated on-site studio, featuring integrated lighting solutions and professional-grade infrastructure, to execute high-polish studio shoots.
Act as a creative partner to internal marketing teams and external agencies to help define and refine the look and feel of our brands.
Audit and maintain our internal equipment identifying the glass, bodies, and lighting needed to meet the cinematic standards of a world-class brand.
Navigate complex industrial environments: utilizing professional lighting techniques to manage high-heat, high-scale manufacturing spaces with precision.
Translate strategic briefs into visual frameworks that keep our motion output steadfast, premium, and scalable.
End-to-End Production
Own the process from the first frame to the final export, moving seamlessly from high-heat industrial environments to the edit suite.
Execute expert-level color grading, pacing, and sound design to ensure every narrative is clear and every delivery is professional.
Balance "A-List" flagship productions with the development of high-quality templates for efficient, quick-turn projects.
Build and maintain a highly organized post-production system: ensuring technical consistency, file management (DAM), and scalable delivery workflows.
Collaborative Partnership
·You must be as comfortable managing a solo shoot as you are collaborating on a two-camera set or dividing post-production tasks.
·Act as a collaborative peer to our existing motion team members, providing mutual creative "pressure-testing" to ensure every frame meets the Miller standard.
·You must be comfortable working in the heat and sparks to catch the authentic moments that cannot be faked.
·Provide technical expertise and creative feedback to partner divisions, ensuring all work, internal or agency-led, lives up to our brand promises.
Qualifications
5+ years of experience in high-end video production and editing within an agency or in-house environment.
In-depth knowledge of the end-to-end video workflow, from storyboarding to pre-production lighting and final delivery.
Mastery of camera systems and professional lighting for industrial spaces.
Advanced proficiency in Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, and After Effects.
A formal degree in Film, Cinematography, Visual Communications, or a related field is preferred, but not required with a proven track record of impactful work.
Foundational knowledge of the welding process or prior experience shooting in industrial/manufacturing environments is a significant plus, but not a requirement.
A portfolio of work must be provided that showcases a versatile range of motion projects from social-first content to cinematic brand storytelling and national spots.
Location and Travel
This role is based at our headquarters in Appleton, Wisconsin, working out of our dedicated production studio.
Expect 20-30% travel for on-location production as project needs dictate.
Candidates must be able to move 25 lbs of gear and work safely around heavy machinery and industrial environments.

practices and product feedback

awareness

insights

Primary Function of Position
The Finance Data Product Analyst will serve as the dedicated FP&A analytics support resource, owning the requirements-to-handoff lifecycle across core FP&A domains. This role fills a current gap where FP&A requirements gathering, stakeholder coordination, and AI-to-engineering handoff are absorbed across leads without dedicated capacity. The analyst will ensure faster turnaround, stronger domain ownership across GLTD, Revenue, CapEx, and HC portfolios, and less rework in downstream deliverables.
Roles and Responsibilities
Serve as the dedicated FP&A analyst for requirements intake — gather, clarify, document, and prioritize business requirements from Finance stakeholders across GLTD, Revenue, CapEx, and HC portfolios.
Translate business requirements into structured technical specifications and data model requirements for handoff to the onsite senior analyst and engineering team.

SQL proficiency for data investigation — ability to query, trace, and validate data across EDW layers (not expected to build pipelines).
Experience with requirements gathering, documentation, and business-to-technical translation.
Familiarity with Snowflake or similar cloud data platforms from an analyst/consumer perspective.
Experience with Tableau or similar BI tools for report validation and basic analysis.
Strong written and verbal communication — ability to write clear specs and coordinate across time zones with onsite teams.
Detail-oriented with a structured approach to tracking deliverables and handoff checklists.

SAP Finance or ERP data familiarity (GL, AP, AR, cost center structures).
Exposure to AI/ML concepts — enough to recognize where AI-assisted analytics could add value to FP&A workflows.
Experience working in offshore delivery models with structured SDLC or agile processes.
Knowledge of data governance and data quality practices.
Required Education and Training
Bachelor's degree in finance, computer science, mathematics, information systems, or business.

title: Embedded Software Engineer - Vison Systems
description:
At Intuitive, we are united behind our mission: we believe that minimally invasive care is life-enhancing care. Through ingenuity and intelligent technology, we expand the potential of physicians to heal without constraints.
As a pioneer and market leader in robotic-assisted surgery, we strive to foster an inclusive and diverse team, committed to making a difference. For more than 25 years, we have worked with hospitals and care teams around the world to help solve some of healthcare's hardest challenges and advance what is possible.
Intuitive has been built by the efforts of great people from diverse backgrounds. We believe great ideas can come from anywhere. We strive to foster an inclusive culture built around diversity of thought and mutual respect. We lead with inclusion and empower our team members to do their best work as their most authentic selves.
Passionate people who want to make a difference drive our culture. Our team members are grounded in integrity, have a strong capacity to learn, the energy to get things done, and bring diverse, real world experiences to help us think in new ways. We actively invest in our team members to support their long-term growth so they can continue to advance our mission and achieve their highest potential.
Join a team committed to taking big leaps forward for a global community of healthcare professionals and their patients. Together, let's advance the world of minimally invasive care.
As an Embedded Software Engineer in the Future Forward organization, you will work at the forefront of innovation, rapid prototyping, and new product development. You’ll collaborate with talented cross-functional teams—including engineers, clinicians, and product managers—to advance Intuitive’s robotic surgical platform, driving the entire product lifecycle from concept to launch.
In this role, you will design, develop, and integrate embedded and platform software across a complex robotic system, interfacing with hardware, firmware, control algorithms, vision pipelines, user interfaces, and test infrastructure, including fault-injection and diagnostic frameworks. You will contribute to the architecture, implementation, and system-level integration of advanced functionalities into complete surgical robotic platforms, supporting product release and validated human use. Your work will be critical to meeting delivery milestones while ensuring safe, reliable, and compliant operation for patients worldwide.
Success in this role requires excelling in an agile, small-team environment—transforming initial concepts into robust prototypes, methodically iterating designs, and consistently maintaining exceptional product quality with a patient-first mindset.
Essential Job Duties
Design and develop robust embedded software to enable system infrastructure, including OS drivers, hardware interfaces, real-time data pipelines, inter-processor communication, error handling, and user/test applications.
Collaborate cross-functionally throughout the product lifecycle with key stakeholders to address clinical needs and safety requirements.
Translate early requirements into prototype implementations to evaluate, iterate, and advance novel robotic systems.
Conduct rigorous unit testing to support system integration and ensure reliable, robust system operation.
Contribute to hazard and failure mode analysis, defining appropriate mitigations.
Refine and iterate designs, balancing technical requirements, feasibility, schedules, and resource constraints.
Produce clear and compliant supporting documentation in alignment with Intuitive's development and quality guidelines.
Ensure all designs meet rigorous quality and safety standards per the Intuitive Quality Management System.
A minimum of 5 years of experience in developing and supporting embedded systems; or 3 years with a Master’s degree; or 1 year with a PhD.
Highly proficient in developing C/C++ embedded and real-time software for multi-core, multi-processor systems, especially on embedded Linux and QNX.
Demonstrated experience with board bring-up, device driver development, and integration of new hardware components.
Skilled in version control systems and collaborative development environments, supporting efficient, iterative improvement.
Familiarity with a wide range of communication protocols—including TCP/IP, CAN, I2C, SPI—and serialization standards such as protobuf.
Strong problem-solving skills and debugging capabilities for complex embedded software and electromechanical systems.
In-depth understanding of failure mode and risk analysis, with a track record in safety-critical, product-focused designs.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills for effective interaction across all organizational levels.
Demonstrates passion for innovation, continuous learning, and developing solutions that make a meaningful difference in patients’ lives.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience with robotics and embedded software for complex electro-mechanical systems.
Knowledgeable in Python or Matlab for automation, diagnostics, and testing.
Familiarity with FPGA development and interfaces.
Familiarity with CUDA programming and memory management concepts.
Cyber-security concepts such as secure boot, authentication and encryption.
Hands-on engineering experience with proven ability to work effectively in a team environment.
Experience in all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, implementation, debug, verification, validation, and transfer to manufacturing.
Experience designing software products in a regulated industry or for mission critical applications; comfort with concepts of design input, design output, traceability, risk analysis, and mitigations.

Architect communication, processing, and distribution of electronic subsystems across the product. Challenge the status quo architecture to propose alternate, efficient and latest tech stacks,
Collaborate on system design and architecture with other Advanced Development engineering team members, including FPGA logic design, mechanical, software and controls.

Implement PCB designs that balance performance, cost, and manufacturability.
Perform board level bring-up and troubleshooting.
Perform formal risk analysis and develop mitigations.
Discover and develop new vendors and their technologies – develop the design and performance understanding to transform these into robust building blocks for future platforms.

The role focuses on developing robust clinical endpoints, defining data collection strategies, establishing data quality and monitoring processes, and supporting the generation of evidence used to evaluate imaging agents, software tools, and future ecosystem applications.
The position serves as a bridge between clinical development, data science, engineering, and external partners, helping ensure that scientific questions are translated into clinically meaningful, measurable, and regulatory-defensible outcomes. The successful candidate will combine expertise in clinical research methodology with a strong understanding of diagnostic performance assessment, clinical data interpretation, and evidence generation in support of innovative surgical technologies.

Support execution of clinical studies evaluating fluorescence imaging agents and ecosystem technologies.
Translate protocol-defined endpoints into operationally executable study procedures and data collection requirements.
Partner with Clinical Development, Data Management, and Biostatistics to ensure endpoint assessments are implemented consistently across sites.
Develop study-specific guidance supporting accurate and reproducible endpoint determination.
Support review of protocols and statistical analysis plans to ensure alignment between study procedures, data collection methods, and endpoint assessments.
Conduct literature reviews and scientific assessments supporting ongoing clinical development activities.

Partner with Data Management to design CRFs, edit checks, and data review workflows.
Define procedures for collection of imaging, pathology, surgical, and clinical outcome data.
Establish data quality metrics and review processes to promote completeness, consistency, and protocol compliance.

Support ongoing review of clinical data throughout study conduct.

Conduct scientific review of emerging study data and identify trends requiring further investigation.
Support blinded image review workflows and centralized assessment activities.

Primary Function of Position
At Intuitive, the needs of our customers are a key driver in our approach to service innovation. Within Global Services Product Management, we build deep understanding of customer needs by working closely with them to assess strengths and opportunities. We incorporate these insights into our Global Service offerings, capabilities, and digital service solutions.
The Senior Product Manager, Global Service Offerings will play a role in Global Services innovation by defining and executing Global Service offering strategy, pricing, portfolio alignment, market research, performance analytics, and commercialization. title: Sr. Embedded Software Engineer
description:
At Intuitive, we are united behind our mission: we believe that minimally invasive care is life-enhancing care. Through ingenuity and intelligent technology, we expand the potential of physicians to heal without constraints.
As a pioneer and market leader in robotic-assisted surgery, we strive to foster an inclusive and diverse team, committed to making a difference. For more than 25 years, we have worked with hospitals and care teams around the world to help solve some of healthcare's hardest challenges and advance what is possible.
Intuitive has been built by the efforts of great people from diverse backgrounds. We believe great ideas can come from anywhere. We strive to foster an inclusive culture built around diversity of thought and mutual respect. We lead with inclusion and empower our team members to do their best work as their most authentic selves.
Passionate people who want to make a difference drive our culture. Our team members are grounded in integrity, have a strong capacity to learn, the energy to get things done, and bring diverse, real world experiences to help us think in new ways. We actively invest in our team members to support their long-term growth so they can continue to advance our mission and achieve their highest potential.
Join a team committed to taking big leaps forward for a global community of healthcare professionals and their patients. Together, let's advance the world of minimally invasive care.
As an Embedded Software Engineer in the Future Forward organization, you will work at the forefront of innovation, rapid prototyping, and new product development. You’ll collaborate with talented cross-functional teams—including engineers, clinicians, and product managers—to advance Intuitive’s robotic surgical platform, driving the entire product lifecycle from concept to launch.
In this role, you will design, develop, and integrate embedded and platform software across a complex robotic system, interfacing with hardware, firmware, control algorithms, vision pipelines, user interfaces, and test infrastructure, including fault-injection and diagnostic frameworks. You will contribute to the architecture, implementation, and system-level integration of advanced functionalities into complete surgical robotic platforms, supporting product release and validated human use. Your work will be critical to meeting delivery milestones while ensuring safe, reliable, and compliant operation for patients worldwide.
Success in this role requires excelling in an agile, small-team environment—transforming initial concepts into robust prototypes, methodically iterating designs, and consistently maintaining exceptional product quality with a patient-first mindset.
Essential Job Duties
Design and develop robust embedded software to enable system infrastructure, including OS drivers, hardware interfaces, real-time data pipelines, inter-processor communication, error handling, and user/test applications.
Collaborate cross-functionally throughout the product lifecycle with key stakeholders to address clinical needs and safety requirements.
Translate early requirements into prototype implementations to evaluate, iterate, and advance novel robotic systems.
Conduct rigorous unit testing to support system integration and ensure reliable, robust system operation.
Contribute to hazard and failure mode analysis, defining appropriate mitigations.
Refine and iterate designs, balancing technical requirements, feasibility, schedules, and resource constraints.
Produce clear and compliant supporting documentation in alignment with Intuitive's development and quality guidelines.
Ensure all designs meet rigorous quality and safety standards per the Intuitive Quality Management System.
A minimum of 5 years of experience in developing and supporting embedded systems; or 3 years with a Master’s degree; or 1 year with a PhD.
Highly proficient in developing C/C++ embedded and real-time software for multi-core, multi-processor systems, especially on embedded Linux and QNX.
Demonstrated experience with board bring-up, device driver development, and integration of new hardware components.
Skilled in version control systems and collaborative development environments, supporting efficient, iterative improvement.
Familiarity with a wide range of communication protocols—including TCP/IP, CAN, I2C, SPI—and serialization standards such as protobuf.
Strong problem-solving skills and debugging capabilities for complex embedded software and electromechanical systems.
In-depth understanding of failure mode and risk analysis, with a track record in safety-critical, product-focused designs.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills for effective interaction across all organizational levels.
Demonstrates passion for innovation, continuous learning, and developing solutions that make a meaningful difference in patients’ lives.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience with robotics and embedded software for complex electro-mechanical systems.
Knowledgeable in Python or Matlab for automation, diagnostics, and testing.
Familiarity with FPGA development and interfaces.
Familiarity with CUDA programming and memory management concepts.
Cyber-security concepts such as secure boot, authentication and encryption.
Hands-on engineering experience with proven ability to work effectively in a team environment.
Experience in all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, implementation, debug, verification, validation, and transfer to manufacturing.
Experience designing software products in a regulated industry or for mission critical applications; comfort with concepts of design input, design output, traceability, risk analysis, and mitigations.

Evaluate and select OEMs and system integrators based on technical capabilities and project requirements.

Provide technical guidance and mentorship to engineers, technicians, and cross-functional project team members.

Experience with high volume automation lines.
Fundamental understanding of process engineering, equipment, test and the manufacturing environment “Self-starter” attitude and comfort in a hands-on environment, where he/she can demonstrate an ability to work with other engineers to influence product design to improve reliability
Demonstrated experience designing and releasing manufacturing equipment or complex automated systems into production.
Proficiency in 3D CAD and engineering drawing development. SolidWorks experience is preferred.
Strong understanding of mechanical design, mechanism development, GD&T, tolerance analysis, material selection, and manufacturing processes.
Ability to integrate mechatronic components such as robotics, sensors, motors, pneumatics, motion control, and machine vision systems.
Experience developing equipment requirements and detailed technical specifications for automation OEMs or system integrators.
Experience reviewing supplier concepts, designs, drawings, component selections, and equipment acceptance plans.
Experience with equipment qualification, process validation, and regulated quality systems.
Strong analytical, troubleshooting, project execution, and technical documentation skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Self-motivated, able to take initiative, and effective in a multidisciplinary team environment.
Required Education and Training
BS/MS degree in Mechanical engineering or a related engineering discipline.
Minimum of eight years of relevant experience developing manufacturing equipment or automation systems.
Direct experience in medical device manufacturing is required.
Staff-level consideration will require additional technical depth and demonstrated leadership of complex equipment or automation projects.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience in an ISO 13485 regulated medical device manufacturing environment.
Experience designing equipment for high-volume assembly of medical devices or precision products.
Experience managing internally designed equipment and externally sourced turnkey automation systems.
Experience with OEM selection, technical bid evaluation, design reviews, factory acceptance testing, site acceptance testing, and production qualification.
Familiarity with design controls, risk management, engineering change control, and equipment validation.
Experience with Windchill and Agile product lifecycle management systems is a strong plus.
Experience mentoring engineers or establishing equipment design standards and engineering best practices.

6+ years of experience in medical technology implementation, IT consulting, or digital within healthcare
Deep understanding of cloud-hosted SaaS platforms, healthcare data security, and networking infrastructure
Experience with account management or direct collaboration with capital sales
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with all levels of stakeholders – operational, clinical, and technical

Bachelor’s Degree

Comfortable working a flexible dynamic schedule.
Remote work

title: Analyst, Regulatory Affairs (State Engagement)
description:
Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future.
Invenergy follows a hybrid schedule, working in office Monday through Thursday and remotely on Fridays if work permits.
This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window.
Job Description
Position Overview
As an Analyst, Regulatory Affairs, you will be responsible for supporting Invenergy's regulatory monitoring and filing activities before state utility commissions, state environmental agencies, and other regulatory bodies across the MISO, SPP, and Southeast regions. Reporting to the Manager, Regulatory Affairs (Central), you will assist in tracking regulatory proceedings, preparing summaries and materials, and coordinating across internal teams to support the advancement of Invenergy's regulatory initiatives.
Key Responsibilities
Monitor state public utility commission, environmental agency, and related regulatory proceedings, filings, orders, rulemakings, and stakeholder activities under the direction of senior team members
Assist in tracking regulatory developments affecting the company's existing assets, development pipeline, and future business opportunities
Maintain an organized regulatory calendar and flag critical deadlines, hearings, workshops, comment periods, and commission decisions for the team's review
Prepare draft summaries of regulatory developments for review by senior staff, including basic notes on implications, risks, and upcoming actions

• Cleans small machine components, as needed.

• Monitors equipment controls, temperature meters, valves and adjusts as needed.

• Records data pertaining to work completed, ingredients used, lot codes and other processing information.
• Assists in cleaning equipment and lines between recipes.
• Very occasionally obtains ingredients/supplies from warehouse.
• Obtains samples of batches and taste test.
• Asks lead, supervisor or material handler if there is any rework.
• Uses rework if there is any consistently.
• Determines ingredients required for formula/recipe and the required amount.
• Ability to safely lift 50lbs on a regular basis.
• Obtains ingredients from storage area or around work area and pours into kettle.
• Meters in other ingredients as required by watching meters and turning on/off kettle.
• Utilizes drum lift by strapping drum into lift and operating hydraulic lift with chain.
• Manually pushes drum lift to kettle and dumps drum of ingredients as needed.
• Operates controls to activate mixers and equipment.
• Monitors controls, equipment temperature, valves, and adjusts equipment to meet formula requirements.
• Hoses spills off floor and hoses towards drains.
• Obtains, measures and weighs additional ingredients to set aside in preparation for next batch or recipe.
• Assists other processors in pouring ingredients into kettles as needed.
• Collects samples and tests for pH, acidity, viscosity and solids.
• Reads test results and adjusts equipment/recipe accordingly.
• Notifies lead processor of any major adjustments needed, or problems with process.
• Transfers finished products to drum, tote, or tank by pumping through piping system.
• Operates switches to control pumps when batch is complete.
• Assists in preparing drums, totes, or tanks for storage of product by ensuring that the proper placarding information is on the package.
• Determines appropriate size of batch needed to accommodate orders and line.
• Closely monitors batch temperature while processing and waiting for packaging to ensure that product will not set prematurely.
• Operates equipment in a safe manner following GMP guidelines and keeps work area clean.
• Supports the Jacksonville plant FSQ and QRMP initiatives on any and all procedures/programs pertaining to product safety.
• Participates in meetings and have scheduling flexibility.
• Trains others as necessary.
• Fills in for other positions as necessary.
• Occasionally testing batches in the lab and recording information on proper documentation.
