Job Overview:   The Kraft Heinz Company is currently seeking an Apprentice Refrigeration Technician to work at our food processing facility in Newberry, SC! Successful candidates must be willing to supply improvements, suggestions, and ideas to help continue the success of our facility. Ideal individuals must be safety and quality orientated along with demonstrate adaptability and willingness to work in a team orientated, fast paced work environment. This position requires troubleshooting, maintenance, and repair of plant refrigeration and steam generation equipment, building and supporting facilities. Involvement in the planning and execution of installation, alteration and modification of existing and new equipment.
Essential Functions & Responsibilities     Respond to plant calls relating to refrigeration system processing deficiencies. Perform analysis of equipment operation and production methods to determine problem. Develop and implement solutions to return to proper operation conditions. Develop and implement solutions to reduce and eliminate reoccurring problems in a systematic manner. Investigate plans and execute maintenance work requests in a timely and cost-effective manner. Scope of work includes but is not limited to repair, alteration and design of thermal, electrical, mechanical, pneumatic, hydraulic, chemical and biological systems.       Consults with plant personnel regarding the required or suggested equipment and facility repair and alteration. Prepares mechanical work requests to repair equipment, building and support facilities. Prepares purchase requisitions to procure needed materials for the completion of work requests. Consults with vendors to procure mechanical supplies, troubleshoot equipment problems and improve plant processes. Prepares material disbursement requisitions and enters time into SAP to accurately document costs for the completion of mechanical work requests. Plans and execute preventative maintenance work requests. Updates exist and write new preventative maintenance routines to effectively improve equipment reliability. Performs daily operational checks on refrigeration and steam generation equipment. Performs daily checks on cooler temperatures to ensure compliance with plant program. Performs daily inspection of plant fire protection and compressed air systems. Monitors usage of plant water, gas and electricity. Actively participates in the PSM process and project teams. Other duties as assigned.
Physical Requirements: Mechanics will spend most of the shift (8-12 hours) on their feet. They must service equipment in the plant, on the grounds, and in support buildings. This covers an area of over 50 acres. This necessitates an excellent deal of walking on wet/slippery floors and working on concrete/asphalt surfaces. Mechanics are encouraged to wear tool pouches on their waist while working (approximately 15 pounds). Mechanics must climb on, over, under or through equipment, catwalks, railings, utility runs, small access doors, etc. Mechanics work in tight spaces under or between equipment, in crawl spaces above the ceiling and inside “confined spaces”. While in these areas, they must lift, lower or support equipment, as well as exert significant force on hand tools. title: Sr. Manager, Procurement Risk & Resilience
location: Chicago/Aon Center, Illinois, United States of America
description:
Job Purpose
The Senior Manager, Procurement Risk & Resilience leads the North America Procurement risk management and resilience strategy and owns responsible sourcing compliance for the region. This role owns the frameworks, governance, tools and cross-functional routines used to identify, assess, prioritize, monitor and mitigate supplier, material, financial, operational, regulatory, geopolitical, quality and sustainability-related risks, while driving supplier compliance with applicable SEDEX requirements.
The position partners closely with Category Procurement, Business Units, Supply Chain, Operations, R&D, Finance, Legal, Food Safety & Quality and Sustainability teams to embed risk into category strategies, sourcing decisions and supplier relationship management. The role strengthens supply continuity, improves decision quality and supports uninterrupted delivery of the company strategic and growth objectives.
Job Description
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
1. Risk & Resilience Strategy and Operating Model
Own and annually refresh the North America Procurement Risk & Resilience roadmap and three-year strategic plan, aligned with business priorities and ambitious risk-reduction targets.
Define the procurement risk operating model, including risk appetite, governance routines, intake and prioritization, KPI tracking and leadership escalation pathways.
Build capability roadmaps covering future-state tools, process improvements, automation opportunities and data enhancements.
Continuously improve risk frameworks, methodologies and controls based on business needs, emerging threats and lessons learned.
2. Material, Supplier and Supply Continuity Risk
Own the Material Risk Assessment methodology and annual AROP cycle, including methodology refresh, category engagement, risk scoring, mitigation planning and progress tracking.
Identify and refine the variables used to measure risk so that the highest-priority materials, suppliers and exposures are targeted for mitigation.
Lead third-party risk management across strategic and critical suppliers, monitoring financial, operational, quality, regulatory, ESG, geographic and geopolitical risks.
Partner with category teams to develop and advance mitigation plans, including alternate sourcing, dual sourcing, contingency planning and other resilience solutions.
Develop procurement resilience playbooks, conduct scenario planning and disruption simulations, and support crisis response and business recovery during supply disruptions.
Maintain accurate material risk trackers and optimize their usability, data quality and relevance for decision-making and reporting.
3. Responsible sourcing
Own North America Procurement’s SEDEX compliance program, governance and annual priorities, aligned with global requirements and business needs.
Manage supplier registration, site association and required information in SEDEX, partnering with category teams and suppliers to address gaps and maintain accurate records.
Monitor supplier and site compliance, track completion against established requirements and follow up on overdue or incomplete actions.
Coordinate with Sustainability, category teams and suppliers on SEDEX related issues, escalations and remediation actions.
Maintain SEDEX compliance dashboards and reporting, providing leadership with visibility to coverage, gaps, progress and priority actions.
Develop guidance and training to support consistent SEDEX compliance across North America Procurement.
4. Risk Decision Support and Category Enablement
Serve as the primary Procurement Risk point of contact for North America category teams and emerging risk issues, coordinating rapid assessment, stakeholder alignment and response recommendations.
Build and maintain a catalog of tools, templates and risk profiles that enable category teams to incorporate risk into category strategies, sourcing strategies, supplier reviews, SRM activities and joint business plans.
Lead regular category risk reviews, provide ad hoc guidance and troubleshooting, and drive mitigation progress against established KPIs.
Assemble cross-functional teams and create situation-specific decision frameworks to prioritize and address complex or critical risk exposures.
5. Cross-Functional Governance and Business Partnership
Lead governance routines with Supply Chain, Operations, Food Safety & Quality, R&D, Finance, Legal, Sustainability and other partners, integrating cross-functional risks that may affect supply continuity.
Partner with Business Units to prioritize critical mitigation projects, align resources and ensure the risk agenda supports strategic business objectives.
Present risk exposure, mitigation progress and priority decisions through BU performance routines and to senior Procurement and business leadership.
Strengthen procurement governance controls, monitor remediation and corrective actions, ensure compliance with policies and regulatory requirements, and support internal and external audits.
6. Digital Risk Intelligence, Data and Reporting
Lead the implementation and continuous improvement of procurement risk technologies, predictive analytics and automated monitoring capabilities.
Integrate relevant internal and external intelligence sources into risk processes and decision-making.
Build executive-ready dashboards and reporting that provide visibility to material and supplier risk exposure, mitigation pipelines, priority projects and performance against targets.
Own country-of-origin mapping capability and governance, including data refresh cadence, data ownership, collection standards, system integration and cross-functional use cases.
7. Communication, Training and Adoption
Develop and maintain annual stakeholder communication and engagement plans, including North America and Global Procurement risk updates.
Maintain the Risk Hub on Proc Connect so current tools, templates, guidance and training materials are accessible and ready for use.
Develop and deliver training on material and supplier risk, and maintain playbooks, SOPs and best-practice documentation to standardize processes and enable scalable adoption.
Drive adoption of Procurement Risk tools, dashboards, templates and practices across North America Procurement and support future deployment of the methodology to other regions.
Required Qualifications
Education
Bachelor’s degree in business, Supply Chain, Procurement, Sustainability, Engineering, Operational Excellence or a related field.
Experience
6-9 years of experience in Procurement, Supply Chain, Risk Management or a related business function.
Demonstrated experience leading supplier or material risk programs and applying third-party risk management frameworks.
Experience in CPG, food manufacturing or another regulated industry preferred.
Experience implementing or managing risk technology platforms and analytics solutions.
Technical Skills
Strong knowledge of supplier and material risk management, business continuity planning, SEDEX compliance, financial risk monitoring, regulatory compliance and crisis management.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capability, with the ability to connect data, risk exposure and business impact.
Proficiency with analytics and visualization tools; experience with Power BI, Tableau or similar platforms preferred.
Understanding of AI-enabled monitoring, automation and emerging digital risk capabilities.
Leadership & Behavioral Competencies
Acts as Procurement’s risk subject-matter expert and trusted advisor.
Influences without authority and builds alignment across senior, cross-functional stakeholders.
Communicates complex risk topics clearly and leads executive communications during disruptions.
Demonstrates strong project management, organizational and stakeholder-management skills.
Balances strategic thinking with disciplined operational execution.
Brings curiosity, sound judgment, a continuous-improvement mindset and a willingness to challenge the status quo.

title: Utilities Supervisor
location: Garland Plant, Texas, United States of America
description:
Lead and coordinate all utility-related activities to ensure maximum operational reliability and compliance in a food and beverage manufacturing facility. This role focuses on safe operation of critical utilities, preventive and predictive maintenance, and continuous improvement initiatives aligned with KHMS pillars (Work Management, Asset Strategy, Failure Elimination) and SMRP best practices.
Key Responsibilities
Safety & Compliance: Enforce safety protocols including Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), confined space entry, and PPE requirements.
Ensure compliance with OSHA, EPA, PSM/RMP, GMP, HACCP, and QRMP standards.
Oversee compliance for ammonia refrigeration, boiler systems, and wastewater treatment.
Support internal and external audits and lead corrective actions.
Assist with safety training, monthly safety meetings, member of safety committee, and provides technical support for all safety projects
Utilities Operations & Reliability: Direct building utilities and maintenance personnel to ensure optimal operation of steam, refrigeration, compressed air, water, wastewater systems, building fabric upkeep, dock doors, ramps, roofs, walls, floors and overall grounds maintenance.
Monitor and record utility usage; report trends and anomalies to ESG teams.
Implement preventive and predictive maintenance programs for building and utility systems.
Assist in troubleshooting and diagnosing malfunctions in all buildings and utility equipment.
Continuous Improvement: Drive initiatives to improve reliability and reduce downtime through equipment modifications and process improvements.
Ensure that equipment and facility are maintained in a safe, operable condition and/or arrange for replacement/upgrades.
Participate in Lean, Six Sigma, and KHMS initiatives to optimize energy efficiency and sustainability.
Analyze downtime reports and initiate action plans to increase efficiency.
Planning & Coordination: Collaborate with planners and other supervisors to ensure accurate job plans and resource allocation.
Verify spare parts availability and coordinate with MRO team for critical spares.
Assist in developing and managing departmental budgets and capital projects.
Leadership & Training: Supervise building and utilities staff, including performance management and employee development.
Provide technical training on utility systems, CMMS usage, and safety compliance.
Promote a culture of accountability, teamwork, and continuous learning.
Critical Skills & Competencies: Strong knowledge of ammonia refrigeration, boiler systems, compressed air, and wastewater treatment.
Familiarity with CMMS platforms (SAP preferred).
Understanding of KHMS and SMRP frameworks for reliability and asset management.
Communicate with outside agencies i.e. contractors, equipment suppliers, technical consultants and vendors.
Ability to lead cross-functional teams and manage change initiatives.
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs): Utility System Uptime: ≥ 99% availability for critical utilities.
Preventive Maintenance Compliance: ≥ 98% completion of scheduled PM tasks.
Energy Efficiency: ≥ 5% annual reduction in energy consumption per production unit.
Unplanned Downtime Reduction: ≥ 15–20% annual reduction for utility-related failures.
PSM/RMP Compliance: 100% adherence to regulatory requirements.
Work Order Accuracy: ≥ 95% compliance with documentation standards.
Training Completion: 100% of utilities team trained on KHMS and reliability fundamentals annually.
Cost Avoidance: Track annual savings from avoided failures and improved energy efficiency.
Safety Compliance: Zero safety violations during utility operations.

Join the LEGO® Brand Retail team as a Seasonal Sales Associate (Brick Specialist) at Fritz Farm in Lexington, KY and provide inspirational guest experiences in an interactive and vibrant store environment. Brand Manager – eCommerce and Brand Building
Are you passionate about building iconic brands and shaping the future of digital commerce?  As a Brand Manager - eCommerce and Brand Building, you will be the driving force behind our growth, seamlessly blending traditional brand management with an “eCommerce-first” mindset.
Reporting to the Portfolio Marketing VP, we are hiring a Brand Manager - eCommerce and Brand Building, who is responsible for leading the holistic strategy for a defined pet nutrition portfolio.  In this highly visible role, you will act as a strategic growth accelerator, managing the business end-to-end, leading a core brand segment holistically or pioneering white-space expansion through innovative new business development.  You will accelerate brand market share and category growth across all channels, with a specialized focus on pure-play and omnichannel retail partners.  Join us to connect cross-functional teams, unlock new growth opportunities, and deliver on our most ambitious brand and eCommerce goals!
What are we looking for?
Bachelor’s degree required; business, marketing, analytics, economics, or a related field is preferred.

title: Technologist, Quality & Food Safety
description:
Job Description:
The Technologist, Quality & Food Safety (Q&FS) is responsible for ensuring all relevant Q&FS standards are implemented and continuously improved to assure quality and food safety at the local site, protecting the consumer and our brands. Operating at the intersection of systematic compliance and factory floor execution, this role provides the hands-on technical expertise needed to identify, mitigate, and control biological, chemical, and physical hazards before they impact our products or consumers.
What are we looking for?
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in food science, Microbiology, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, a closely related scientific discipline or equivalent
2+ years in a food or related manufacturing facility, with hands-on experience in HACCP, food safety management systems, and internal auditing.
Strong ability to lead Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and write clear, audit-ready technical procedures.
Strong technical courage to confidently halt production or hold inventory, alongside excellent communication skills to coach floor operators.
Ability to stand and walk the manufacturing floor for prolonged periods of time, working safely around high-speed machinery in hot, dusty, or noisy plant environments.
10% travel
Preferred Qualifications
Active HACCP, HARPC, or PCQI (Preventive Controls Qualified Individual) certification
FSSC 22000 internal auditor certification
High proficiency in Microsoft Office; direct experience with SAP
What will be your key responsibilities?
Standards & Regulatory Alignment : Ensure all site processes and procedures strictly comply with corporate Mars Quality and Food Safety Standards, Business Unit directives, and regulatory agency regulations.
HACCP & Risk Management:  Serve as a core Food Safety Representative for the site HACCP Team and Food Safety Team, leading and supporting risk assessments for all facility changes (CAB, new products/packaging/processes) and validating Critical Control Points (CCPs).
Incident & Hold Management:  Manage the site product hold-and-release programs within SAP, NCMGT, and Nexus. Ensuring proper isolation, disposition, and destruction of non-conforming materials and products.
Audit & CAPA Leadership:  Supports site internal audits and Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) programs to drive continuous system improvements.
Incident Response & RCA:  Serve as a PRIMP (Product Related Incident Management Process) owner, leading structured root-cause analysis (RCA) sessions and recommending corrective actions.
Continuous Improvement:  Works to identify defects and trends in site processes.  Develop and/or lead improvement projects in alignment with the Site Q&FS Manager.
Capability & Training:  Develop and deliver interactive food safety and GMP training modules to build technical capability and a strong quality culture among site associates.
Finished Product Release:  Execute the final release of finished products, ensuring all quality and food safety specifications have been met.
Other Duties: assigned by the Site Quality and Food Safety Manager

Work with diverse and talented Associates, all guided by The Five Principles.
Join a purpose driven company, where we’re striving to build the world we want tomorrow, today.
Best-in-class learning and development support from day one, including access to our in-house Mars University.
An industry competitive salary and benefits package, including company bonus.

title: Critical Environment Technician
description:
Overview
As a Critical Environment Technician in Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) team, you will maintain the critical infrastructure that keeps our Datacenters up and running. This could be anything from coordinating with supplier/vendors, recognizing safe versus unsafe work environment, having a hands-on understanding of how critical environment equipment works, performing various types of maintenance, responding to onsite incidents while coordinating with other critical facilities professionals, and using telemetry and other platforms to monitor equipment performance and operations.
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role’s job duties.
Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture
Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed and promotes a safe working culture to empower less experienced team members. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance
Prepares and submits required reports (e.g., turnover, preventative maintenance [PM]) as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates, or using ad hoc methods required to support trending and analysis (e.g., Maintenance data, equipment trending data). Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for devices and disciplines within their coverage and expertise to ensure safe and reliable execution. Documents completed work using approved tools and procedural templates for more experienced technician review. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments. Analyzes findings from reports and documents observations.
Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs following methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for multiple disciplines and one or more types of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, cooling systems) with minimal supervision - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Performs maintenance tasks and repairs that can be performed with minimal oversight. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Oversees maintenance tasks within a single discipline or area of expertise. Maintains all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance with established mastery of maintaining systems of a specific discipline.
Provides necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site based on the appropriate procedure levels of risk (LOR). Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Recognizes circumstances when to stop supplier/vendor work to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates per appropriate LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Coordinates and schedules supplier/vendor on-site activities. Reviews and completes appropriate work orders to support approval of vendor supplier field service reports or invoices.
Processes method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Coordinates activities and associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities.
Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Determines when troubleshooting efforts are deemed adequate and communicates or escalates to suppliers, engineers, or more experienced colleagues as needed. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment works within disciplines they have been trained and how to troubleshoot to a subsystem level. Provides consultation to less experienced colleagues with troubleshooting systems and problems. May lead efforts to troubleshoot issues and identify root causes.

Works on advanced tasks (e.g., vendor contact, escalations) independently. Serves as a subject matter expert in critical environments-related systems within the data center, and advises less experienced colleagues on such topics. Possesses an understanding of and operates equipment and systems within a set discipline (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls) with knowledge of the interactions between them and overall operation of a data center. Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
Inspects and supervises critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds for unsafe or abnormal conditions to develop and analyze trends. Understands critical system alarms for single discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) within the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify all alarms. Uses technical expertise, prior experience, and device analytics to recognize trends with equipment behavior and checks potential issues as they arise. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems. Performs all monitoring equipment repair, replacement, and maintenance work, which meets or exceeds Microsoft Service Level Agreement (SLA) requirements.
Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks hours for performed tasks within applicable task management systems. Adds required data, documents, logs changes, and upkeeps procedures related to building management systems and reports. Properly signals spare equipment and parts utilization within maintenance work orders.
Safety and quickly responds to and leads an onsite incident response team for all abnormal conditions that impact operations, and coordinates with other critical facilities professionals to perform corrective repairs, without supervision. Gathers necessary information and creates incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies and contacts/engages appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur. Develops new or follows preexisting emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Directly provides emergency monitoring response to irregular or malfunctioning conditions.

Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg. with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.

Background Check Requirements:

Associate's Degree or technical trade certification (e.g., military, trade school), or higher-equivalent education OR High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent AND 1+ year(s) technical services experience (e.g., high-availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical) OR equivalent experience.

description:
Overview
Job Description
Overview:
Microsoft Cloud Operations and Innovation (CO&I) is the team behind the cloud.  Within CO&I, the Datacenter Engineering (DCE) team is responsible for delivering core datacenter infrastructure for Microsoft’s cloud business. The MS portfolio consists of complex, multi-disciplinary, large scale, multi-year datacenter construction and lease projects. We are looking for a passionate, high-energy individual to help build the cloud datacenters that power the world’s largest online services.
In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.
Responsibilities
Responsibilities:
The Datacenter Engineering Technical Program Manager will support the delivery and technical oversight of short-term AI Infrastructure-as-a-Service contracts across the AMER region. This role will focus on evaluating the technical readiness, compliance, and ongoing performance of third-party datacenter infrastructure supporting high-density AI/GPU deployments.
•    The Technical Program Manager will serve as a primary engineering interface between Microsoft and external providers, coordinating across regional engineering, operations, construction, networking, and other technical stakeholders.
•    The role will support technical feasibility assessments for prospective sites, engineering audits of existing facilities, and troubleshooting of infrastructure issues at operational sites.
•    A strong electrical or mechanical engineering background is critical for this position. The Technical Program Manager must be able to evaluate mission-critical infrastructure serving high-density compute environments, identify technical risks and gaps, engage the appropriate engineering SMEs, and drive issues through resolution.
•    The role will manage multiple projects concurrently, coordinate external architecture and engineering resources, manage technical consulting contracts, and ensure that technical documentation and site information are complete and ready for engineering review.
Core Responsibilities:
•    Lead technical audits and compliance assessments of third-party datacenter facilities supporting AI infrastructure service contracts.
•    Perform and coordinate technical feasibility assessments for prospective AI/GPU sites, identifying infrastructure limitations, risks, required modifications, and engineering gaps.
•    Review provider design documentation and technical information against Microsoft requirements, with particular focus on electrical and mechanical infrastructure supporting high-density compute deployments.
•    Provide technical support and coordinate troubleshooting for existing operational sites, partnering with providers, Microsoft Operations, and engineering SMEs to understand infrastructure issues and drive resolution.
•    Coordinate external architects, engineers, consultants, and technical vendors performing site assessments, design reviews, audits, and engineering studies.
•    Serve as the central technical coordination point between providers and Microsoft engineering, operations, networking, site acquisition, and other internal stakeholders.
•    Identify technical gaps, risks, dependencies, and decisions required to determine site feasibility and readiness.
•    Coordinate with Microsoft electrical, mechanical, controls, telecom, and other engineering SMEs on discipline-specific technical issues.
•    Maintain technical documentation, audit findings, risk registers, action items, and project information within applicable portfolio tools and document repositories.
•    Develop and present regular portfolio-level reporting covering site readiness, audit findings, technical risks, outstanding issues, and required decisions.
•    Coordinate technical site visits, including engineering participants, documentation requirements, audit scope, and readiness activities.
•    Track external provider and engineering consultant deliverables, responsiveness, documentation quality, and closure of technical issues.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
Bachelor's Degree AND 4+ years experience in engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development OR equivalent experience. 2+ years of experience managing cross-functional and/or cross-team projects.. Other Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.
Citizenship Verification: This position requires verification of US Citizenship to meet federal government security requirements.
Preferred Qualifications:
•    10+ years of experience in mission-critical or high-tech infrastructure such as datacenters, semiconductor facilities, large-scale manufacturing, pharmaceutical facilities, or oil and gas.
•    Electrical engineering experience with utility/service capacity, MV/LV distribution, transformers, switchgear, UPS systems, generators, grounding, protection, and critical-load power distribution.
•    Mechanical engineering experience with chilled-water systems, heat rejection, pumps, cooling distribution, controls, and high-density cooling systems.
•    Experience assessing infrastructure supporting high-density AI or accelerated-compute environments.
•    Experience performing site feasibility assessments, technical due diligence, design reviews, facility audits, and engineering studies.
•    Experience supporting root-cause analysis and troubleshooting electrical or mechanical infrastructure issues within operating mission-critical facilities.
•    Experience working with third-party datacenter, colocation, hosting, or infrastructure service providers.
•    Knowledge of commercial contracts, technical exhibits, provider obligations, and contractual remedies.
•    Knowledge of the AMER datacenter and third-party infrastructure market.
Demonstrated electrical and/or mechanical engineering expertise in mission-critical infrastructure, including the ability to independently evaluate engineering designs, system capacity, redundancy, reliability, technical risks, and infrastructure limitations.
•    Experience performing technical due diligence, engineering feasibility assessments, design reviews, technical audits, or similar evaluations used to determine infrastructure readiness and risk.
•    Ability to review engineering documentation, identify technical risks and gaps, and coordinate resolution across multiple engineering disciplines.
•    Experience working with technical vendors, engineering consultants, contractors, or infrastructure providers.
•    Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex engineering issues into clear risks, actions, and decisions.
•    Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and priorities in a fast-paced environment.
•    Demonstrated ability to work effectively across technical and non-technical organizations and with both internal and external stakeholders.

title: Graphics Software Engineer II
description:
Overview
Windows Servicing and Delivery (WSD) has core mission of keeping customers and Windows ecosystem protected and productive, delivering monthly Windows updates to 1+ billion devices running different versions of Windows Operating System. Graphics team is part of WSD and responsible for keeping Windows Graphics components secure and reliable in existing and future versions of Windows by working closely with our product teams, partners and customers. The team owns all the Graphics stacks like DirectX, Graphic Device Interface (GDI) and GDI+ for servicing by fixing security, reliability, performance and functional issues in existing and future versions of Windows while owning GDI and GDI+ for future development.
We are a team of engineers passionate about product security and quality, care deeply about bringing the best customer experience to our products while ensuring a great Win32 experience to users on a diverse set of devices.
We are looking for a Graphics Software Engineer II that would like to learn the internals of Windows platform, enjoy solving customer problems, passionate about modernizing Windows code and help us to deliver on our core mission. This position offers a unique opportunity to enhance technical skills, get deeper understanding of how software works end to end and accelerate your career growth with a high accent on security.
At Microsoft, our mission—to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more—guides how we partner with customers to deliver trusted, impactful solutions. With a growth mindset culture, we innovate responsibly and measure success by shared progress—people, teams, and customers. Join us to do meaningful work that changes the world and helps shape what’s next for everyone.

Analyze and address security defects in Windows reported by security researchers.
Root cause analysis of functional and security code defects, performance problems in Windows. Generalize the findings and create solutions to address the defects.
Design, proto-type new features in GDI; ship new features on the next version of the Operating System.
Learn the design and implementation details of a substantial part of the Windows code base.
Analyze the code base through static and dynamic analysis tool.
Be part of AI efforts to modernize existing tools and processes or build new ones from scratch.

Required Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 2+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python. OR equivalent experience.

Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.
Preferred Qualifications
Problem-solving, debugging and troubleshooting skills.
Coding experience in C/C++ in a professional capacity.
Ability to design and implement robust system architectures and frameworks.
1+ years of experience in performing regression testing.
Ability to prioritize and handle multiple tasks.
Familiarity with kernel mode debugging through WinDbg.
Familiarity with 2D graphics algorithms.
Experience with telemetry, data analysis and visualization.
Working knowledge of static and dynamic analyzers.
Familiarity with TrueType, Open Type, Variable Fonts specifications.
Experience of working through multiple full product cycles.

title: Incident Response Program Manager
description:
Overview
The Trust and Integrity Protection (TrIP) organization helps Microsoft’s commercial business grow with trust by translating security, privacy, data-protection, regulatory, and operational risks into clear decisions, effective controls, and measurable outcomes.
The TrIP Incident Response team provides incident-response capabilities for in-scope security, privacy, and data-protection events affecting Microsoft’s commercial business. The team assesses reported events, coordinates containment and remediation, supports regulatory and customer-notification decisions, maintains incident evidence, and works with engineering, legal, privacy, security, and business stakeholders through closure.
We are looking for a Incident Response Program Manager to join the TrIP Security Incident Response team. This role will provide hands-on incident coordination and program-management support across a global operating model, strengthening coverage and the team’s ability to respond to high-priority and concurrent incidents.
The successful candidate will help triage, contain, investigate, document, and resolve incidents while coordinating stakeholders and ensuring actions are completed within applicable incident-response, regulatory, contractual, and customer-notification requirements.
The role will also support operational readiness, process improvement, metrics, post-incident learning, and the controlled use of automation technologies. This is a hands-on role for someone who combines security knowledge, technical program management, sound judgment, operational discipline, and the ability to work effectively through ambiguity.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Protect customers and the business
Support timely containment of active or potential data exposure, gathering and validating facts needed to assess customer impact, affected data, impacted environments, geographic considerations, and potential harm.
Coordinate with privacy, legal, security, engineering, business, and customer-facing stakeholders to evaluate regulatory, contractual, and notification requirements.
Help ensure that time-sensitive requirements and internal service commitments are identified, tracked, escalated, and completed.
Support specialized incidents involving delivery partners, restricted environments, government information, and other scenarios that require additional handling controls.
Coordinate incident response
Triage reported events to determine scope, severity, ownership, required stakeholders, and immediate response actions.
Drive incidents through containment, investigation, remediation, notification assessment, evidence collection, and closure.
Coordinate high-priority or non-routine incidents that require rapid escalation, specialized engagement, or authoritative Microsoft decisions.
Maintain clear ownership, timelines, dependencies, decisions, and next actions throughout the incident lifecycle.
Participate in a shared on-call rotation providing incident-response coverage.
Drive disciplined case management
Maintain complete, accurate, and audit-ready incident records in approved case-management systems.
Document verified facts, incident decisions, stakeholders, remediation actions, approvals, communications, evidence, and closure rationale.
Monitor active cases, aging, escalations, blockers, response commitments, and required follow-up actions.
Coordinate across engineering and business teams to resolve dependencies and keep incidents progressing toward closure.
Help identify recurring incident patterns, control weaknesses, process gaps, and broader risks discovered through incident investigations.
Translate operational findings into actionable remediation recommendations and track agreed actions to completion.
Improve incident-response operations
Analyze operational data and case trends to identify opportunities to improve response quality, speed, consistency, and stakeholder experience.
Contribute to incident-response metrics, dashboards, reporting, service reviews, and leadership updates.
Develop and maintain runbooks, decision trees, escalation paths, templates, operating procedures, and readiness materials.
Participate in post-incident reviews, tabletop exercises, and continuous-improvement activities.
Help ensure that operational changes are introduced with defined ownership, documented controls, appropriate testing, and measurable outcomes.
Partner with vendors and internal teams while maintaining clear Microsoft accountability for governance, exceptions, approvals, and high-risk decisions.
Support the controlled operation and continued improvement of AI solutions and related incident-response automations.
Build trusted partnerships
Establish effective working relationships with security, privacy, legal, engineering, support, business, risk, compliance, and customer-facing teams.
Communicate incident status, risks, blockers, decisions, and required actions clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Facilitate structured discussions during high-pressure situations and drive stakeholders toward clear decisions and accountable actions.
Operate effectively across global teams, cultures, organizations, and time zones.
Handle sensitive and confidential incident information with appropriate discretion and care
Embody our  culture  and  values
Qualifications
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree AND 2+ years experience in engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development OR equivalent experience. 1+ year(s) of experience managing cross-functional and/or cross-team projects.
Preferred Qualifications
The candidate is a hands-on incident responder and technical program manager who:
Is comfortable moving between detailed case execution and broader operational improvement.
Communicates clearly with technical teams, legal and compliance partners, business leaders, and customer-facing stakeholders.
Uses data and operational evidence to identify patterns and improve controls, processes, and readiness.
Takes ownership and maintains high standards for quality, confidentiality, and auditability.
Experience managing multiple workstreams, stakeholders, dependencies, risks, and deadlines in a complex environment.
Ability to gather technical and business information, distinguish verified facts from assumptions, and translate findings into clear actions.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document decisions, operational processes, and technical issues clearly.
Ability to work through ambiguity, adjust priorities during active incidents, and maintain effective execution under time-sensitive conditions.
Ability to participate in a shared on-call rotation, including support outside standard business hours when required.
Experience coordinating incident triage, containment, investigation, remediation, evidence collection, or post-incident reviews.
Familiarity with incident and case-management platforms such as ServiceNow, or comparable systems.
Experience developing or improving operational procedures, runbooks, escalation paths, metrics, dashboards, and service-management processes.
Experience partnering with engineering teams to manage defects, operational dependencies, production readiness, and automation.
Familiarity with regulatory, contractual, customer-notification, or government-environment considerations affecting incident response.
Has experience leading AI-powered transformation initiatives, including the implementation of agentic workflows, automation, and data-driven solutions at enterprise scale.

title: Operations Key Account Manager
description:
Overview
Microsoft partners are central to how Microsoft reaches and serves customers. The Partner Enablement organization, within Microsoft Business Operations, helps partners understand, prepare for, implement, and adopt changes across the partner lifecycle.
The role independently leads complex, cross-functional partner enablement programs that bridge Microsoft strategy and partner execution. The Operations Key Account Manager develops a deep understanding of partner business models, capabilities, dependencies, and operational experiences; translates partner insight into clear recommendations and actionable business requirements; identifies and communicates risks early; and drives readiness and adoption for priority launches and change moments. Acting as a trusted advisor and Voice of Partner, this role is expected to create clarity in ambiguous situations, influence decisions without direct authority, and deliver measurable outcomes that reduce friction, strengthen trust, and improve the ease of doing business with Microsoft.
Scope
Operates independently on complex programs with broad cross-functional dependencies and material partner or business impact.
Moves from analysis to a clear point of view, recommendation, and action plan; uses sound judgment to make progress when direction is incomplete.
Leads through influence rather than formal authority, aligning stakeholders on outcomes, ownership, decisions, and timelines.
Anticipates risks and dependencies, escalates with context and options, and drives issues to resolution with appropriate urgency.
Communicates concise, decision-ready updates for leadership and adapts detail for partner, technical, operational, and executive audiences.
Creates reusable approaches, operating rhythms, standards, and scalable solutions that improve outcomes beyond a single launch or partner.
Leads the partner-facing change-management workstream from early impact assessment through sustained adoption, while keeping ownership of product, policy, platform, and technical delivery with the originating teams.
Facilitates structured co-design among partners, engineering, product, business planning, operations, and launch teams to test assumptions, shape requirements, validate implementation feasibility, and resolve readiness risks before launch commitments are finalized.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond
Responsibilities
Partner Lifecycle Enablement and Trusted Advisory
Drive partner enablement across end-to-end partner lifecycle processes to reduce friction and improve the ease of doing business with Microsoft.
Build trusted relationships and structured engagement rhythms that surface partner priorities, operational pain points, requirements, risks, and emerging needs.
Develop a practical understanding of partner business models, capabilities, technical and operational dependencies, and change impacts.
Translate complex Microsoft business, product, engineering, policy, security, compliance, and platform changes into clear partner actions and operational implications.
Voice of Partner and Advocacy
Represent the Voice of Partner across Microsoft, using partner evidence and subject-matter expertise to influence requirements, design, prioritization, roadmaps, and launch decisions.
Assess, clarify, and prioritize partner requirements, converting partner asks into actionable business requirements, recommendations, or experience improvements.
Clearly articulate partner risks and concerns, including tangible business and operational impact, required ownership, and mitigation or risk-acceptance decisions.
Connect individual partner experiences to broader patterns and systemic opportunities, and close the feedback loop with partners and internal stakeholders.
Partner Co-Design and Engineering Collaboration
Plan and facilitate co-design engagements with representative partners and engineering teams for changes that meet defined impact, complexity, or risk criteria.
Frame clear co-design objectives, partner scenarios, decision questions, constraints, and expected outputs so sessions produce actionable evidence rather than general feedback.
Translate partner workflows, technical dependencies, implementation effort, and operational constraints into prioritized requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, or design recommendations for engineering and business owners.
Partner with engineering and product owners to identify what can be influenced, what is fixed, and what requires an explicit trade-off, exception, or risk-acceptance decision.
Coordinate previews, pilots, sandbox or test-environment validation, and implementation walkthroughs to confirm that guidance, tooling, APIs, support paths, and operational processes are usable before broad release.
Document decisions, owners, unresolved issues, and feedback disposition; close the loop with participating partners by explaining what changed, what did not, and why.
Readiness, Adoption, and Change Management
Own the partner change-management and readiness plan for priority launches and key change moments, including the change narrative, impacted partner segments, required partner actions, deliverables, milestones, dependencies, measures of success, risks, communications inputs, and stakeholder updates.
Assess change impact and cumulative change burden across partner business models, geographies, roles, technical architectures, operational processes, and overlapping implementation timelines; identify where sequencing, scope, or support must change.
Define readiness criteria and evidence for each change, distinguishing confirmed preparedness, at-risk status, not-ready status, and unknown status; use these signals to inform launch, mitigation, escalation, and exception decisions.
Escalate blockers early with clear business impact, accountable ownership, and resolution needs; drive mitigation before critical milestones and go-live.
Track implementation and adoption through and after go-live, confirm whether required partner actions and intended outcomes were achieved, and transition unresolved issues or sustained support needs to accountable owners.
Data, Scale, and Continuous Improvement
Use preparedness, adoption, operational, business, and qualitative data to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and systemic gaps.
Define measurable success criteria and deliver concise, decision-ready executive narratives that include a clear assessment, recommendation, trade-offs, and actions required.
Apply a continuous-improvement mindset to standardize services, simplify processes, reduce manual work, and advance automation, AI-enabled insights, and self-service enablement models.
Balance high-touch partner engagement with scalable and preventative solutions that address recurring friction across the broader ecosystem.
Cross-Functional Leadership
Demonstrate a One Microsoft approach by working seamlessly across engineering, business planning, product and launch, sales, operations, support, compliance, and enablement teams.
Create clarity on accountability, decisions, and next steps; independently convene and align the right stakeholders to solve ambiguous, cross-organizational problems.
Influence without direct authority using partner evidence, sound judgment, business impact, and data; confidently recommend a path forward when information is incomplete.
Demonstrate thought leadership, strategic thinking, adaptability, and proactive identification of end-to-end opportunities that drive business impact.
Success in This Role
Partners understand the change, know what actions are required, and are prepared to implement and adopt it with greater confidence and less friction.
Partner requirements and risks are surfaced early enough to influence design, launch, process, policy, or operational decisions.
Readiness plans provide an honest, timely view of progress, dependencies, blockers, ownership, and decisions required.
Partner insights are translated into measurable improvements and scalable solutions rather than repeated one-off interventions.
Cross-functional teams have clear accountability and shared understanding of partner impact, priorities, and outcomes.
Representative partners and engineers have validated critical scenarios, requirements, technical guidance, and implementation paths early enough to influence the solution or make explicit risk decisions.
Readiness status is evidence-based, distinguishes known risk from unknown status, and drives timely decisions on sequencing, mitigation, exceptions, and launch confidence.
Change-management plans address partner awareness, understanding, capability, implementation, adoption, reinforcement, and closed-loop learning rather than stopping at communications or launch completion.
Embody our  culture  and  values
Qualifications
Minimum / Required Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Business, Operations, Finance, or related field AND 4+ years experience in program management, process management, or process improvement OR equivalent experience.
Preferred Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Business, Operations, Finance, Supply Chain, Technology, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field AND 8+ years of relevant experience, OR equivalent experience.
Experience working in global, cross-functional, and highly matrixed environments.
Proven record of delivering complex programs, launches, operational changes, or improvement initiatives with competing priorities.
Demonstrated experience in partner channel management, partner operations, customer relationship management, customer success, or strategic account engagement.
Ability to translate technical, operational, and business requirements into clear plans, recommendations, and executive-ready communications.
Strong project and change-management capability, including change-impact assessment, stakeholder and resistance planning, readiness criteria, adoption measurement, navigating ambiguity, resolving conflict, negotiating trade-offs, and developing practical solutions.
Strong analytical capability using data, reporting, dashboards, KPIs, and qualitative insight to influence decisions and monitor outcomes.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex subjects to global audiences and engage effectively across levels and cultures.
Demonstrated impact and influence skills, including cross-boundary collaboration and relationship building with internal and external stakeholders.
Experience identifying systemic issues and applying industry practices, standardization, automation, AI, continuous improvement, or self-service solutions to improve scale and sustainability.
Understanding of cloud, commerce, digital platforms, partner ecosystems, security, compliance, or lifecycle operations is advantageous.
Independent, flexible, proactive, and able to identify strategic opportunities, develop proposals, and gain stakeholder alignment.
Core Capabilities
Partner Advocacy and Voice of Partner | Partner Co-Design and Engineering Collaboration | Strategic Business Analysis | Program and Change Management | Readiness and Adoption | Data-Informed Decision Making | Risk Management | Executive Communication | Cross-Functional Influence | Relationship Management | Continuous Improvement | Automation and Scale

The Americas Channel organization leads Microsoft's channel partner strategy and execution across the United States, Canada, and Latin America, working through partner types including Distributors, Scale Solution Providers, Telcos, and SME&C Solution Integrators to accelerate customer adoption of Microsoft AI and Cloud. As the Americas Channel Telco Partner Type Lead, you own the Telco partner strategy for the region and sit at the leading front of partner performance for one of our most strategic and fastest transforming partner types.

The daily responsibilities will include the following:
Review, scope, investigate, advocate for, and solve customer challenges/issues, collaborating within and across teams

Match the urgency of the customer and always maintain calm, professional attitude, functioning as the face of Microsoft and the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program
Consistently leverage delivery tools, processes, and methodologies to ensure the good partner experience and accurate case coding
Follows up consistently and intentionally, and develops action plans for resolving customer escalations
Help drive partner satisfaction by providing accurate information, prompt callbacks, and timely follow-ups on all action items
Communicate effectively and leave a good impression as the first point of contact
Provide end-to-end management of Microsoft Partner requests and remove as much effort from the partner experience as possible

Microsoft Defender, Microsoft Sentinel, and Microsoft Entra reaches Product Engineering and gets resolved. Working within a shared, organization-wide framework for triage, prioritization, delivery to Engineering, and feedback updates, you will lead a cross-functional virtual team that brings product management discipline and deep support expertise to in-market feedback, covering both incident and non-incident items. You will give customer-facing and Product Engineering teams one clear view of status, decisions, and outcomes, and help peer product managers apply the same approach across other security product areas.
Microsoft Purview and Microsoft Intune in market. You will bring product management and support expertise to lead feedback on generally available capabilities from intake to closure, working with support, customer-facing, partner, and Product Engineering teams across organizations to bring signals together, confirm patterns, prioritize issues, and drive clear decisions. You will engage customers directly when firsthand context will sharpen a decision.
You will bring together post-launch input from support trends, incidents, customer-facing teams, product usage, and research; use AI-assisted analysis to group related feedback, identify patterns, and support prioritization; determine whether an issue is a product gap or a configuration, integration, or operational challenge; and turn the findings into actionable recommendations for Product Engineering. You will drive tradeoff decisions across quality, supportability, and product improvement, using evidence and human judgment so customer priorities are handled consistently across Microsoft Security.

You have built and operated a customer feedback or product-insights process that multiple teams adopted, used technical and business evidence to shape engineering decisions, and influenced Product and Engineering without direct authority. You bring product judgment, deep understanding of customer support and escalation workflows, technical depth in enterprise security and cloud architectures, and a record of driving qualified feedback from intake through engineering decision and follow-up with customer-facing teams. Engineering teams trust the quality of your analysis, and peers rely on you to make the feedback process consistent, data-driven, and fair. The specific product areas may change with business needs, but the purpose remains the same: bring post-launch signals together, deliver what matters most to Product Engineering, and close the loop.

Industry Solutions Delivery (ISD) is a global organization of over 8,000 strategic sellers, industry experts, elite engineers, architects and consultants, working together to bring Microsoft’s mission of empowerment – and cutting-edge technology - to life for the world’s most influential customers.
As a Regional Partner Commercial Leader - Industry Solutions Delivery (Americas)  you will own the end-to-end commercial engagement with delivery partners in your region. Reporting to the ISD Partner Leader, this role drives Microsoft’s FY26 ISD partner strategy at the regional level – managing partner utilization and accelerating commercial cloud growth  through effective partner selection, contracting, negotiating and performance management. You will lead a team of Partner Commercial Individual Contributors and work cross-functionally with sales and delivery teams to build a high-performing, curated partner ecosystem that delivers customer success while meeting ISD’s profitability and growth targets.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Partner Selection & Contracting
Serve as the regional expert on partner engagement during deal pursuits, acting as an impartial advisor on selecting the “right partner for the right work” based on capability and capacity.
Lead negotiations with chosen subcontractor partners before deal closure – structuring scope, pricing, and contract terms that align with the deal’s needs and ISD’s financial targets.
Ensure subcontractor agreements mirror customer contract requirements (e.g. milestones, SLAs, Ts&Cs flow downs) so that partners are accountable under the same conditions.
Uphold compliant sourcing processes (e.g. running mini-RFPs among vetted partners when required) to justify partner choices and adhere to governance standards.
Outcome: Optimal partner arrangements are secured for each deal, balancing competitive pricing with protections for margin and cloud consumption objectives.
Delivery Oversight & Partner Performance
Once projects are underway, act as the single point of ownership for partner performance across all ISD engagements in your region. Oversee partners at a macro level – monitoring delivery outcomes (timeliness, quality, compliance) and reviewing partner scorecard KPIs (e.g. quality ratings, Azure consumption, NNR, ECIF ROI) across programs.
Conduct regular performance checkpoints and lead regular executive reviews with each key partner to assess results and future plans.
Drive continuous improvement: if a partner underperforms or misses deliverables, work with their leadership on remediation plans and escalate within ISD as needed; conversely, recognise and champion high-performing partners to grant them more opportunities.
Manage ongoing commercial aspects post-sale, such as negotiating any rate card adjustments or resolving commercial issues based on performance and market benchmarks.
Outcome: A consistently high level of partner delivery excellence is maintained (measured by partner quality scores and successful project outcomes), and issues are proactively addressed to protect customer success and ISD’s margins.
Drive Cloud Growth via Partners
Align every partner engagement with Microsoft’s cloud growth ambitions.
Work with deal teams to embed consumption-focused incentives and outcome-based elements into partner contracts, ensuring partners are motivated to deliver projects faster and drive Azure usage (e.g. milestone bonuses linked to cloud adoption).
During delivery, track and maximise Azure Consumption Revenue (ACR) generated by partner-led projects, intervening if consumption lags and replicating best practices from partners who accelerate cloud adoption.
Partner Ecosystem & Strategy Execution
Execute the FY26 ISD Partner Strategy in your region by focusing partner investments on a selective set of trusted, high-performing partners.
Rationalise the long-tail of vendors by guiding internal teams to use approved strategic partners and enforcing exception processes for any new/unvetted suppliers.
Partner with Partner Operations and Compliance to ensure any new partners are onboarded and managed in line with global standards and processes, providing a consistent experience for both internal stakeholders and partners.
Collaborate closely with the ISD Partner Leader and other regional Partner Commercial Leads to share learnings, maintain strict governance, and continually refine commercial frameworks (rate cards, templates, incentive models) that protect Microsoft’s interests while enabling partner success.
Outcome: A streamlined, strategic partner ecosystem that delivers at scale without compromising on quality or gross margin. Internally, sellers and delivery teams have a clear, efficient process to engage partners; externally, partners find it easy and rewarding to do business with ISD, fostering stronger alliances.
Team Leadership & Collaboration
Manage and mentor a regional team of Partner Commercial ICs, providing direction and ensuring consistency in how they support deals and projects.
Set clear objectives for your team around partner deal structuring and delivery oversight.
Foster a culture of data-driven decision making – using partner performance metrics (e.g. Partner Value Index scores, consumption dashboards) to guide actions.
Coordinate with other leaders (sales, solutioning, delivery management, and the central Partner Operations & Compliance team) to remove blockers and continuously improve partner engagement processes across the region.
Outcome: Your team operates as an effective “hub” for partner-related matters in the region, and stakeholders feel supported and aligned in executing the partner strategy.
Other
Embody our  culture  and  values
Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Business, Operations, Finance, or related field AND 8+ years experience in program management OR equivalent experience.
6+ years management (e.g., people, project, process, vendor, change) experience.
Additional or preferred qualifications Master's Degree in Business, Operations, Finance, or related field AND 12+ years experience program management OR Bachelor's Degree in Business, Operations, Finance, or related field AND 15+ years experience in program management
OR equivalent experience.
8+ years people management experience.
10+ years in enterprise technology partner management, consulting, or outsourcing roles.
Experience in structuring large subcontractor agreements or alliances and managing vendor/partner performance at scale.
Experience in cloud services is highly desirable (familiarity with Microsoft Azure and services business a strong plus).
Commercial & Negotiation Skills: Required negotiation and contract management skills, with the ability to craft complex deal terms that balance risk and reward.
Understanding of various commercial models (T&M, fixed-price, outcome-based) and how to apply them to drive desired outcomes.
Adept at financial analysis, pricing strategies, and ensuring gross margin objectives are met in partner-engaged deals.
Strategic Thinking: Ability to translate high-level partner strategy into operational execution.
Experience in optimising a partner ecosystem – e.g. selecting the right mix of global vs. local partners, leveraging economies of scale, and implementing governance to ensure compliance.
Ability to make data-driven decisions on partner usage (when to engage partners, in what capacity) aligned with business goals.
Leadership & Collaboration:
Able to work cross-functionally – partnering with sales leaders, delivery project managers, contracting/legal, finance, and partner management offices.
Required communication and stakeholder management skills, to represent partner interests in internal forums and to represent Microsoft’s interests in tough partner negotiations.
Results & Performance Orientation: Data-oriented and outcome-focused, with experience setting and measuring KPIs.
Experience in using dashboards and scorecards to monitor partner performance (e.g. delivery quality, on-time delivery, customer satisfaction, consumption metrics) and to hold partners (and internal teams) accountable.

Human-centered AI for  affective and social computing,  and adaptive experiences.
Situated interaction  between humans and AI systems such as robots deployed in the physical world.
Conversational AI Agents  that are  socially  and context aware.
