title: Senior Critical Environment Technician
description:
Overview
As a  Senior Critical Environment Technician (SCET) in Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) team, you will maintain the critical infrastructure that keeps our Datacenters up and running. This could be anything from coordinating with supplier/vendors, working closely with Management to address operational, risk and safety situations, mentoring other CE Technicians, having a hands-on understanding on how critical environment equipment works, performing various types of maintenance, responding to onsite incidents while coordinating with other critical facilities professionals, and using telemetry and other platforms to monitor equipment performance and operations.
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role’s job duties.
Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed and promotes a safe working culture to empower less experienced team members. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Proactively assesses and shares current and emerging security threats in safety discussions and shares best practices to address or mitigate risk. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance Processes method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Coordinates activities and associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities. Advises engineer partners or project management colleagues on project scope process or execution methodology. Presents for review and approval MSOW in their area of responsibility.
Prepares and submits highly complex reports as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates, or using ad hoc methods required to support trending and analysis (e.g., Root Cause Analysis [RCA] reports) and may review prior reports delivered by less experienced team members. Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for highly complex and/or interdependent equipment and disciplines to ensure safe and reliable execution. Reviews completed work using approved tools and procedural templates from less experienced technicians for accuracy and completeness. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments. Analyzes findings from reports and documents observations.
Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs for multiple disciplines and multiple equipment types of increasing complexity with no supervision, while serving as a subject matter expert for one discipline - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Incorporates security governance frameworks into maintenance practices and drives continuous security improvements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Provides consultation to colleagues on maintenance and repairs through deep understanding of equipment, systems and their interrelations. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Oversees everyday, complex, large-scale tasks for a single discipline or equipment across disciplines. Ensures follow up action items are addressed in a timely manner. Masters the maintenance of all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance across all disciplines. Plans, coordinates, and presents maintenance items for review and approval in their area of responsibility. Serves as an expert on applying security principles to ensure all systems are protected against unauthorized access during maintenance.
Acts as a subject matter expert, performing troubleshooting independently for multiple equipment, systems, subsystems, and component types. Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Determines when troubleshooting efforts are deemed adequate and communicates or escalates to suppliers, engineers, or more experienced colleagues as needed. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment in all disciplines work and how to troubleshoot to subsystem level. Provides consultation to less experienced colleagues with troubleshooting systems and problems. Oversees less experienced colleagues, or directly troubleshooting systems and investigates root causes. Ensures that security incidents identified during troubleshooting are addressed promptly and escalated as necessary.
Provides necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site based on all procedure levels of risk (LOR), enforcing security requirements for all third-party access and operations. Takes part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Recognizes circumstances when to stop supplier/vendor work to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates across all LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Coordinates and schedules supplier/vendor on-site activities. Coordinates with vendor to schedule maintenance and determines availability of equipment/parts, as directed. Resolves or escalates observed vendor quality issues. May review and approve vendor supplier field service reports, invoices, and work orders.
Equipment and Systems Operations Serves as an expert in the inspection and supervision of critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds for unsafe or abnormal conditions. Understands critical system alarms for multiple discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (e.g., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) and understands risks or impacts to other subsystems across the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify all alarms. Uses technical expertise, prior experience, and device analytics to recognize trends with equipment behavior and checks potential issues as they arise. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems. Performs all monitoring equipment repair, replacement, and maintenance work, which meets or exceeds Microsoft Service Level Agreement (SLA) requirements. Uses data trends to develop or produce predictive analyses of equipment performance.
Safety and quickly responds to and leads an onsite incident response team for all abnormal conditions that impact operations, and coordinates with other critical facilities professionals to perform corrective repairs, without supervision. Gathers necessary information and creates incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies and contacts/engages appropriate parties and security points of contact to mitigate incidents as they occur. Develops new or follows preexisting emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Directly provides and/or leads and coordinates emergency monitoring response plans for irregular or malfunctioning conditions. Serves as technical expert in ensuring emergency operating procedures (EOPs) are consistent with proper incident response.
Works on complex, advanced tasks (e.g., stabilization, resolution, recovery) independently. Serves as a subject matter expert in critical environments-related systems within the data center, advises less experienced colleagues on such topics, and provides oversight and training/mentorship to team members on tasks regarding these subsystems (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls, generators). Serves as a resource for less experienced team members to incorporate security-first principles into daily tasks, ensuring all equipment operations prioritize identifying potential security threats and mitigating them immediately. Demonstrates an understanding of and operates equipment and systems across all disciplines (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls) with knowledge of the interactions between them and overall operation of a data center. Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner in alignment with Microsoft standards.
Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work in accordance with all Microsoft security policies. Tracks hours for performed tasks within applicable task management systems. Tracks utilization and time tracking results for team members, within applicable task management systems, as needed. Guides and coaches team in CMMS usage best practices. Adds required data, documents, logs changes, and upkeeps procedures related to building management systems and reports. Properly signals spare equipment and parts utilization within maintenance work orders.
Physical Requirements Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting 50lbs / 22.5kg. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg. with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Working Conditions Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
As indicated above, this role has a travel requirement of up to 25% which means you may be required to travel, from time to time, as part of this role.
As indicated above,   have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Other
Embody our  culture  and  values
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent AND 3+ years mission critical services work/applied learning experience (e.g., high availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or related fields) OR equivalent experience.
1+ year(s) experience in a specialized area (e.g., mechanical field, electrical field, controls field) or related field.
Other Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.
This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Candidates must have authorization to work in the United States that does not now or in the future require employer sponsorship.
Preferred Qualifications:
High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent AND 5+ years mission critical services experience (e.g., high-availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or related fields) OR Associate's Degree or technical trade certification (e.g., military, trade school), or higher-equivalent education AND 4+ years mission-critical services experience (e.g., high-availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or related fields)
OR equivalent experience.

location: United States, Washington, Redmond; United States, California, Mountain View; United States, New York, New York; United States, Georgia, Atlanta
description:
Overview
The Security Compete team helps Microsoft Security win. We turn competitive evidence into sharper positioning, field guidance, go-to-market choices and product input across four pillars: Get Ready for AI, Securing AI, Defend with AI and Securing Data. We partner with product and engineering to shape what we build, so market insight becomes a better product, not just better messaging. From leadership setting strategy to sellers in a live deal, we get people the insight they need to decide and win. AI helps us move at market speed, and our experts stay accountable for every call.
Every AI agent needs an identity, and every AI app runs through the network. That puts identity and network access at the center of securing AI, and every major vendor in the space is racing to lead it.
Your insight will shape how Microsoft wins today and what it builds next. You'll lead competitive intelligence across IAM, identity governance (IGA), ITDR, and Security Service Edge (ZTNA, secure web gateway, CASB), helping Microsoft lead across identity, network access, and securing AI.
Responsibilities
Competitive insight across identity, network access, and securing AI
Identity and network access vendors are expanding into securing AI, from governing AI agents to controlling how people use AI apps. You’ll track how platform and specialist competitors are evolving across IAM, governance, and SSE, and what that means for Microsoft.
Input into Microsoft Entra’s direction
You’ll work with Entra product marketing and engineering to turn that insight into decisions on how Microsoft secures AI agents and AI access: where to invest, what to improve, and how to position. You'll ground recommendations in customer conversations, win/loss analysis, field feedback, and market signals.
Field guidance for competitive evaluations
You’ll build the vendor analyses, technical briefs, and battlecards sellers use against identity, governance, and SSE competitors, including in evaluations focused on securing AI. You’ll support priority deals where competitive insight can change the outcome, using AI to keep pace with the market while staying accountable for accuracy.
Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications
Master's Degree in in Marketing, Computer Science, Business or related field AND 3+ years experience in business OR Bachelor's Degree in Marketing, Computer Science, Business or related field AND 5+ years experience in business OR equivalent experience.
Additional or preferred qualifications
Technical depth in identity and/or network access security, such as SSO/MFA and conditional access, identity governance and lifecycle (IGA), privileged access, ITDR, or SSE/SASE technologies including ZTNA, secure web gateway, and CASB. Deep expertise in both identity and network is not required ; strength in one with curiosity to go deep in the other is ideal.
Familiarity with securing AI, such as agent and non-human identities or AI app access controls, is a plus.
Experience in competitive intelligence, technical product marketing, or structured market evaluation, including designing competitive evaluations, use-case tests, or benchmarks and separating reproducible evidence from vendor claims.
Strong analytical judgment and synthesis skills, with the ability to combine technical, customer, market, and commercial evidence; communicate uncertainty; and translate complex findings into positioning, product recommendations, sales guidance, and executive narratives.
Demonstrated ability to influence across engineering, product, marketing, and sales stakeholders in a matrixed environment, with clear written communication and effective presentations for both technical and executive audiences.
Relevant identity, networking, or security certifications can complement practical experience but are not required .

6+ years’ experience in backend service development, 2+ years’ experience in batch or streaming data processing to process the PiB level data.

We're entering a new era defined by the power of AI to transform how organizations operate and innovate. At Microsoft, we're building the next generation of AI-powered platforms and production-grade solutions that help customers solve complex challenges and create meaningful business impact.
Microsoft Frontier Co. is a new line of business and one of the industry's first customer outcome-driven organizations, bringing together industry expertise, strategic partnerships and engineering as part of MCAPS. Its teams will work side-by-side with customers to co-design, deploy, and continuously improve AI systems that deliver measurable, customer-defined outcomes. The organization is built around end-to-end Frontier Transformation, helping customers turn AI into real, lasting business value. For those joining, it's a chance to help build a new growth engine for Microsoft and shape how the industry moves from delivering technology to delivering outcomes.

Embedded directly with customers, you'll partner closely with stakeholders to understand their most critical challenges and rapidly design, build, and deploy solutions that move from concept to production.

Design and continuously improve the operating mechanisms that enable scalable cloud capacity delivery across a highly matrixed global organization.
Establish governance, decision forums, risk management frameworks, escalation paths, accountability models, and execution rhythms that accelerate outcomes.
Create repeatable processes and operating models that increase delivery speed, predictability, quality, and organizational effectiveness.
Focus organizations on decisions, tradeoffs, risks, blockers, and outcomes rather than status reporting.

Translate business demand and strategic priorities into actionable execution plans with measurable outcomes.
Drive portfolio-level improvements that reduce cycle times, increase decision velocity, and improve delivery predictability.

Facilitate alignment across organizations with differing priorities, constraints, and perspectives.
Build consensus around complex problem statements, evaluate competing options, and help stakeholders converge on a preferred path forward.
Influence and drive outcomes without direct authority by combining technical credibility, business judgment, and trusted relationships.

Lead through uncertainty by defining problems, challenging assumptions, identifying root causes, and framing actionable decisions.
Develop decision-ready recommendations that balance technical realities, business objectives, risk, and long-term strategic considerations.
Make progress despite incomplete information by driving iterative learning and informed decision making.
Continuously challenge the status quo and identify opportunities to simplify, accelerate, and improve existing operating models.

Prepare and deliver executive reviews, strategic recommendations, and decision frameworks for senior leadership.
Translate complex technical and operational challenges into concise, compelling, and actionable business discussions.

Create an environment where the collective capability of the organization exceeds that of any individual contributor.

description:

 - 8+ years engineering complex live, broadcast, and studio production, including high-profile livestreams, public venue events, design, configuration, and programming of physical audio infrastructure, and critical on-location filming or streaming.

 - Proven experience serving as A1 when failures are immediately visible and time for sophisticated workarounds is measured in seconds.

 - Expert command of gain structure, routing, EQ, dynamics, automixing, feedback control, real time noise suppression, mix-minus, IFB, intercom, playback, comms, and latency management.

 - Deep experience designing and troubleshooting redundant program, stream, multitrack, camera, backup-recorder, and archival audio paths.

 - Expert wireless-microphone and RF coordination skills across crowded, high-consequence production environments, including frequency planning, antenna distribution, and intermodulation.

 - Ability to capture exceptional spoken-word audio for keynote presenters, executive livestream hosts, stage panels, podcasts, voiceover, remote guests, and acoustically difficult spaces.

 - Advanced microphone selection and placement skills, including lavalier concealment, boom technique, room treatment, noise control, and feedback prevention.

 - Ability to mix full-duplex speech-to-speech audio between humans and AI models for a variety of different event formats

 - Fluency with broadcast encoders, embedded audio, streaming protocols, conferencing platforms, and external distribution endpoints.

 - Expert-level understanding of room acoustics and a fundamental understanding of acoustic science.

 - Demonstrated success diagnosing and repairing signal-chain, DSP, synchronization, routing, RF, networking, and hardware faults during live production.

 - Strong multitrack recording, timecode, sync, metadata, editing, mixing, delivery, backup, and archival judgment across professional formats and loudness specifications.

 - Functional audio post-production skills, including dialogue cleanup, noise reduction, EQ, dynamics, mix revisions, and delivery preparation.

 - Ability to lead audio crews, support technical freelancers, challenge flawed technical plans, and communicate decisive options under pressure.

 - Willingness to work onsite, travel globally as needed, and support rehearsals or productions outside standard hours when critical productions require it.

This role requires deep Oracle Financials expertise, strong accounting process knowledge, and an engineering mindset. You will work across corporate accounting processes including equity, payroll, accruals, leases, mergers and acquisitions, intercompany, and close; transform Accounts Payable processes; and design solutions for complex supply chain accounting, cost accounting, ASC 606 revenue recognition, and compute and data-center accounting. You’ll help redefine how finance teams work by applying automation, AI, and agentic approaches to reduce manual effort, strengthen controls, and accelerate accounting and close processes.

description:
About the Role

As Head of First Party Chip Finance, you will be the finance leader for OpenAI’s custom silicon efforts. You will partner with teams across chip design, engineering, infrastructure, supply chain, and finance to turn technical roadmaps into sound investment decisions and financially disciplined execution.

This role spans the full chip development lifecycle: evaluating design and roadmap choices, building investment cases, forecasting development and production costs, and supporting manufacturing and deployment at scale. You will give leadership a clear view of program economics, funding requirements, and risks as we build first-party compute capabilities.

In this role, you will:

 - Lead financial evaluation of custom silicon programs, including development investment, production economics, deployment assumptions, and expected returns. Assess first-party chips against alternative compute options.

 - Build and own program-level models and multiyear forecasts that connect engineering milestones, development spending, manufacturing volumes, supplier commitments, and cash requirements.

 - Partner closely with chip-design and engineering leaders on technical decisions that affect performance, power consumption, cost, and time to deployment. Translate complex design tradeoffs into clear financial recommendations.

 - Develop a detailed view of chip and system costs, including wafers, manufacturing yields, packaging, memory, testing, and integration. Identify opportunities to improve economics as programs move from development into production.

 - Partner with Supply Chain and Procurement on supplier strategy and commercial negotiations, including capacity reservations, volume commitments, prepayments, and contractual risk.

 - Work with Treasury, Corporate Finance, Accounting, Tax, and Legal to evaluate financing and payment structures, manage financial exposure, and support program execution.

 - Support commercial deployment and pricing decisions through analysis of unit economics, total cost of ownership, and the relationship between technical performance and economic value.

 - Establish budgets, reporting, and financial controls that give engineering and finance leaders timely visibility into spending, commitments, milestones, and emerging risks. Build a small, high-performing team while remaining directly involved in the analysis.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - Prior experience leading finance for semiconductor or custom silicon programs. You have directly owned investment analysis, program budgets, and financial decisions across chip development and production.

 - An undergraduate degree in a technical discipline, preferably electrical engineering or computer science. An MBA or equivalent business experience complements your technical foundation.

 - 10+ years of experience across semiconductor finance, hardware finance, strategic finance, or related fields, with substantial responsibility for complex technical programs.

 - Strong command of semiconductor economics, including development costs, manufacturing yields, packaging and memory costs, production ramps, and supplier commitments.

 - Excellent financial modeling skills and the ability to independently build models, test technical and commercial assumptions, quantify uncertainty, and recommend a path forward.

 - The technical credibility to work closely with chip designers and engineering leaders, understand their constraints, and evaluate tradeoffs across performance, power, cost, and timing.

 - Experience supporting supplier negotiations, prepayments, and major investment commitments in partnership with supply chain and finance teams.

title: Manager, Return To Vendor (RTV)
description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE IDEAL CANDIDATE:
The Manager, Return to Vendor (RTV) is a key individual contributor within the Sourcing organization responsible for overseeing the end-to-end RTV process across the company's retail and e-commerce supply chain. This role serves as the primary point of contact for vendor return negotiations, disputes, and recovery, ensuring that defective, excess, and non-conforming merchandise is resolved efficiently and that the company maximizes recovery value. The ideal candidate is highly analytical, a skilled negotiator, and comfortable operating cross-functionally with Merchandising, Quality, Logistics, Finance, and Vendor partners.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
RTV Program Ownership
Own and manage the full RTV lifecycle — from claim initiation through resolution, credit receipt, or physical return logistics.
Establish and maintain a centralized RTV tracking system; monitor open claims, aging balances, and recovery rates.
Develop and enforce RTV policies, standard operating procedures, and escalation protocols.
Partner with Buying and Planning teams to identify and prioritize RTV candidates across categories.
Vendor Negotiation & Relationship Management
Lead direct negotiations with vendor partners to secure credits, replacements, or return authorizations in alignment with contractual terms.
Build and maintain productive vendor relationships while assertively advocating for the company's financial interests.
Review and interpret vendor contracts and purchase order terms related to returns, defects, and chargebacks.
Identify recurring quality or compliance issues with vendors and escalate to the Sourcing Director for strategic action.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Collaborate with the Logistics and Warehouse teams to coordinate physical return shipments, disposition of goods, and inbound/outbound documentation.
Partner with Finance and Accounts Payable to ensure timely posting of vendor credits and accurate reconciliation of RTV balances.
Work with the Quality Assurance team to document and report on product defect trends to inform future sourcing decisions.
Support Buying teams during vendor onboarding to ensure RTV terms and expectations are clearly defined.
Reporting & Continuous Improvement
Produce regular reporting on RTV volume, recovery rate, aging claims, and open liabilities for senior leadership review.
Identify process gaps and implement improvements to reduce cycle time, increase recovery, and minimize dispute resolution time.
Benchmark RTV performance against industry standards and recommend best practices.
REQUIREMENTS:
5+ years of experience in sourcing, procurement, vendor management, or supply chain — with direct RTV, chargeback, or vendor compliance exposure.
Demonstrated experience negotiating with vendor partners, including knowledge of contract terms, credit processes, and dispute resolution.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to manage large volumes of data and derive actionable insights.
Proficiency in Google Sheets; experience with ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, or equivalent) and inventory/order management platforms.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to influence without authority across internal teams and external partners.
Highly organized with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple open claims and priorities simultaneously.
All posted ranges are reflective of base salary and may vary depending upon experience level and location. Bonus and equity may also be provided for eligible roles.

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

description: About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. Role Summary The Craftsmanship Auditor evaluates Rivian vehicles from the customer’s perspective to identify, document, prioritize, and help resolve craftsmanship and perceived-quality concerns. This role performs repeatable static and dynamic vehicle audits using approved standards, quality sheets, measurement tools, and audit systems. The auditor is responsible for producing objective, evidence-based findings that help Rivian protect customer experience, maintain build quality, and drive timely corrective action across Manufacturing, Plant Quality, Engineering, Paint, Supplier Quality, and related teams. Responsibilities Perform full and focused craftsmanship audits in accordance with applicable work instructions. Inspect exterior, interior, and vehicle functionality from a customer and trained-observer perspective. Perform static inspections and dynamic road tests, including evaluation of fit and finish, gaps and flush, closures, trim, paint, molding, interfaces, comfort, ergonomics functionality, wind noise, road noise, and other customer-facing attributes. Identify defects objectively and compare conditions against current boundary criteria, Craftsmanship Quality Sheets, gap plans, design intent, benchmarking references, and other approved standards. Use approved inspection and measurement equipment, including feeler gauges, gap-and-flush gauges, radii gauges, force gauges, calipers, and related tools. Create clear, accurate, and complete defect records in the Rivian Craftsmanship Audit systems, including vehicle identification, location, condition, evidence, severity, and issue ownership.. Review audit findings with the team lead and relevant stakeholders to confirm defect description, classification, severity, and ownership. Escalate safety or regulatory concerns, and other high-impact issues through the established escalation process. Provide objective photos, measurements, observations, and other evidence needed for root-cause analysis and corrective actions Participate in daily startup meetings, defect walk-throughs, calibration activities, team all-hands, and required training. Support continuous improvement of audit methods, reporting, equipment, and craftsmanship standards. Maintain a safe, organized, and professional audit area consistent with PPE, 5S, and Rivian standard-work expectations. Qualifications High school diploma or equivalent. Experience in automotive manufacturing, vehicle repair, quality inspection, craftsmanship, or a related technical field. Ability to inspect vehicles carefully and consistently using visual, tactile, auditory, and functional observations. Ability to read and apply technical standards, quality criteria, work instructions, and measurement results. Ability to use or learn inspection tools such as gauges, calipers, force gauges, and gap-and-flush measurement equipment. Basic understanding of manufacturing quality concepts, defect containment, corrective action, and root-cause problem solving. Ability to accurately document findings using digital systems such as Google sheets, and power point presentations Strong attention to detail and ability to distinguish objective defects from acceptable variation. Clear written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams. Ability to follow safety requirements, PPE requirements, standard work, and controlled audit procedures. Preferred Qualifications Experience performing vehicle-level craftsmanship, perceived-quality, end-of-line, or customer-readiness audits. Experience with automotive fit and finish, body, paint, interior trim, closures, or vehicle functionality. Experience with manufacturing execution systems, quality dashboards, or digital inspection tools. Ability to interpret basic engineering drawings, gap plans, or dimensional requirements. Work Environment and Physical Requirements This is an on-site role in a fast-paced vehicle manufacturing and audit environment. Work requires frequent standing, walking, reaching, and use of hands to handle tools and vehicle components. Work may require bending, kneeling, crouching, stooping, climbing stairs or ladders, and working around vehicles at varying heights. The role may require close visual inspection and the ability to adjust focus while evaluating vehicle surfaces, interfaces, and components. Role Summary This position is designed for emerging to mid-level Technicians who are eager to grow their technical acumen while delivering an exceptional customer experience. The ideal candidate thrives in dynamic, fast-paced environments, possesses strong communication skills, and brings a passion for innovation and adventure. While based primarily at a local service center, this role may involve remote work, traveling for mobile service, or supporting plant operations as business needs evolve. Responsibilities Vehicle Service & Repair: Perform or assist with assigned vehicle diagnosis, repairs, installations, and inspections—whether at a service center, mobile route, or remote location. Procedure & Safety Adherence: Utilize available technical resources and follow repair procedures efficiently without compromising quality or safety. Quality Assurance: Conduct road tests on vehicles post-repair to verify repair quality and ensure operational safety. Parts & Operations Management: Assist with day-to-day parts operations, including ordering, receiving, shipping, inventory tracking, and work order/expense reporting. Documentation: Maintain proper, detailed technical notes and documentation for all completed and in-process repairs for internal and external use. Customer Interaction: Perform duties with high professionalism when interacting with customers, families, third-party affiliates, and suppliers at service facilities or outreach events. Continuous Improvement: Identify process areas for improvement, provide constructive feedback to mentorship leads, and participate in service campaigns or containment initiatives. Professional Growth: Actively engage in required training, stay current on evolving technical skills, and maintain high-quality work with minimal supervision as experience increases. Qualifications General & Operational Requirements: High School Diploma, GED, or recognized equivalency credential preferred. Minimum age of 21 years old. Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record (no suspensions or revocations within the past 3–5 years). Ability to drive a non-commercial truck and trailer is preferred. Availability for a standard 40-hour workweek, including potential shifts on weekends, holidays, early mornings, evenings, or overnights based on business needs. Flexibility for travel to regional locations or production facilities as needed. Proficient with laptops/computers in Windows or Mac environments, as well as work order management systems. Eagerness to learn, strong organizational skills, time management, and high attention to detail. Ability to perform physical tasks, including sitting, standing, walking, bending, kneeling, reaching, and lifting up to 50 lbs. Education & Experience: Graduation from an accredited automotive repair school/program is highly preferred. 0–3 years of hands-on experience in an automotive shop or technical environment; open to recent graduates looking to launch their career. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary This position is designed for emerging to mid-level Technicians who are eager to grow their technical acumen while delivering an exceptional customer experience. As part of our junior talent pipeline, you will work closely under the mentorship of senior technicians and leadership to support EV repairs, inspections, and field service operations. The ideal candidate thrives in dynamic, fast-paced environments, possesses strong communication skills, and brings a passion for innovation and adventure. While based primarily at a local service center, this role may involve remote work, traveling for mobile service, or supporting plant operations as business needs evolve. Responsibilities Vehicle Service & Repair: Perform or assist with assigned vehicle diagnosis, repairs, installations, and inspections—whether at a service center, mobile route, or remote location. Technical Guidance & Learning: Learn to identify and explain the product line, EV framework, tools, and accessories while establishing peer relationships and working under the mentorship of senior technicians. Procedure & Safety Adherence: Utilize available technical resources and follow repair procedures efficiently without compromising quality or safety. Quality Assurance: Conduct road tests on vehicles post-repair to verify repair quality and ensure operational safety. Parts & Operations Management: Assist with day-to-day parts operations, including ordering, receiving, shipping, inventory tracking, and work order/expense reporting. Documentation: Maintain proper, detailed technical notes and documentation for all completed and in-process repairs for internal and external use. Customer Interaction: Perform duties with high professionalism when interacting with customers, families, third-party affiliates, and suppliers at service facilities or outreach events. Continuous Improvement: Identify process areas for improvement, provide constructive feedback to mentorship leads, and participate in service campaigns or containment initiatives. Professional Growth: Actively engage in required training, stay current on evolving technical skills, and maintain high-quality work with minimal supervision as experience increases. Qualifications General & Operational Requirements: High School Diploma, GED, or recognized equivalency credential preferred. Minimum age of 21 years old. Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record (no suspensions or revocations within the past 3–5 years). Ability to drive a non-commercial truck and trailer is preferred. Availability for a standard 40-hour workweek, including potential shifts on weekends, holidays, early mornings, evenings, or overnights based on business needs. Flexibility for travel to regional locations or production facilities as needed. Proficient with laptops/computers in Windows or Mac environments, as well as work order management systems. Eagerness to learn, strong organizational skills, time management, and high attention to detail. Ability to perform physical tasks, including sitting, standing, walking, bending, kneeling, reaching, and lifting up to 50 lbs. Education & Experience: Graduation from an accredited automotive repair school/program is highly preferred. 0–3 years of hands-on experience in an automotive shop or technical environment; open to recent graduates looking to launch their career. Technical Foundations (Junior Level Focus) Electrical & Systems: Foundational understanding of basic electricity theory (high voltage vs. low voltage awareness), basic circuit measurement tools (DVOM), and introductory exposure to reading electrical schematics. Role Summary This position is designed for emerging to mid-level Technicians who are eager to grow their technical acumen while delivering an exceptional customer experience. Customer Interaction: Perform duties with high professionalism when interacting with customers, families, third-party affiliates, and suppliers at service facilities or outreach events. Professional Growth: Actively engage in required training, stay current on evolving technical skills, and maintain high-quality work with minimal supervision as experience increases. Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record (no suspensions or revocations within the past 3–5 years). Ability to drive a non-commercial truck and trailer is preferred. Availability for a standard 40-hour workweek, including potential shifts on weekends, holidays, early mornings, evenings, or overnights based on business needs. Flexibility for travel to regional locations or production facilities as needed. Proficient with laptops/computers in Windows or Mac environments, as well as work order management systems. Eagerness to learn, strong organizational skills, time management, and high attention to detail. Ability to perform physical tasks, including sitting, standing, walking, bending, kneeling, reaching, and lifting up to 50 lbs. Are you passionate about  Global Finance & Accounting?  S&C Electric Company is seeking a dynamic individual to join our Global Finance and Accounting team. As Director-Global Accounting,  you’ll be crucial in ensuring continued innovation and supporting our diverse team.
The Director, Global Accounting is responsible for overseeing the company's international accounting operations and ensuring timely, accurate and efficient financial close, reporting and accounting execution across multiple regions.  This role provides leadership for global accounting standardization, internal controls, process excellence, organizational effectiveness and readiness for global tax reporting requirements, including accounting support for OECD Pillar II and transfer pricing matters.
The position serves as a key leader for corporate accounting operations and acts as a strategic partner to the Vice President, Finance in support of financial reporting, operational excellence, financials controls, and organizational transformation initiatives.
Key Responsibilities:
Global Accounting Leadership
Oversee the company's international accounting operations across manufacturing and non-manufacturing locations.
Establish consistent accounting processes, close procedures, and governance across regions.
Develop and executive the accounting organization's strategic roadmap.
Ensure alignment of accounting practices with corporate objectives and business requirements.
Support a high-performing international accounting organization focused on accuracy, accountability, controls and continuous improvement.
Financial Close & Reporting
Oversee the monthly, quarterly and annual financial close processes across international entities.
Ensure timely and accurate financial reporting in accordance with U.S. GAAP and local statutory requirements.
Drive balance sheet integrity through robust reconciliation and review processes.
Oversee preparation and review of management reporting packages and supporting schedules.
Ensure compliance with all internal and external financial reporting deadlines.
International Accounting Oversight
Provide leadership and governance for international accounting operations.
Ensure compliance with local accounting, tax and statutory reporting requirements.
Coordinate activities across regional accounting teams to drive consistency and efficiency.
Partner with Tax to support OECD Pillar II readiness, including Globe data requirements, jurisdictional effective tax rate reporting, statutory reporting implications, and related accounting controls.
Lead transfer pricing compliance through accurate intercompany accounting, reconciliations, cost allocations, related-party balance support and timely documentation of cross-border transactions.
Process Improvement & Standardization
Identify opportunities to streamline, automate, and standardize accounting processes.
Implement best practices across close, accounting reconciliations, reporting and transaction processing.
Partner with Finance Transformation and Systems teams on ERP, automation and digitalization initiatives.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives that reduce cycle times and improve quality.
Audit & Compliance Support
Coordinate annual audit activities across international locations.
Lead internal control compliance efforts and management testing activities across international entities.
Ensure timely resolution of audit findings and recommendations.
Coordinate with tax, legal and external advisors on audit support for OECD Pillar II, statutory tax accounting, transfer pricing documentation and cross-border intercompany matters.
Business Partnership
Partner closely with FP&A, Treasury, Tax, Payroll, and Operations leaders.
Support acquisitions, integrations, restructuring activities and strategic initiatives.
Assist executive leadership with financial analysis and decision support.
Provide accounting data governance and decision support for transfer pricing policies, intercompany profit allocations and global minimum tax compliance requirements, in partnership with tax.
Talent Development
Develop future accounting leaders through coaching and mentoring.
Foster collaboration and knowledge-sharing across the global accounting organization.

Bachelor's Degree in Accounting or Finance
12+ years of progressive accounting leadership experience.
Experience leading multi-national accounting organizations in a manufacturing environment.
Strong background in financial reporting, cost accounting, and global close processes.
Experience managing accounting teams across multiple countries.
ERP implementation or finance transformation experience preferred.
Experience supporting multinational tax compliance processes preferred, including transfer pricing, intercompany accounting, statutory reporting, and OECD Pillar II.
Expert understanding of U.S GAAP and financial reporting requirements.
Strong knowledge of multinational accounting operations.
Experience managing distributed teams across multiple regions.
Demonstrated ability to lead organizational change and process improvements.
Strong executive communication and leadership capabilities.
Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.
Working knowledge of OECD Pillar II requirements, including GloBE data considerations, jurisdictional reporting needs, accounting controls and the finance function's role in supporting global minimum tax compliance.
Strong understanding of transfer pricing principles, intercompany accounting, related-party transaction governance, and documentation support for cross-border arrangements.
Proven ability to balance strategic priorities with operational execution.

Join Our Team as a Lead Generator Specialist!
Are you passionate about  Electrical and Mechanical Laboratories?  S&C Electric Company is seeking a dynamic individual to join our Electrical and Mechanical Labs team. As a Lead Generator Specialist,  you’ll be crucial in ensuring continued innovation and supporting our diverse team.
The Lead Generator Specialist is responsible for improving maintenance programs for the lab’s short-circuit generators, their controls, and related auxiliary equipment. This role involves collaborating with cross-functional teams, developing test equipment, test methods, analyzing test data, and providing insights to support product development and quality improvement efforts. The Specialist is expected to coach other team members to ensure their development, and skills retention in the lab. The Specialist will report to Senior Manager – NJC Laboratories.
Key Responsibilities:
Perform technical inspections on, create plans for and lead preventative maintenance of, and assess the performance of short-circuit generators and their drive systems.
Develop preventative maintenance strategies, assessment strategies, and implement those strategies for generator stators, rotors, electric windings, insulation, controls, and instrumentation.
Lead efforts to troubleshoot issues, and apply standard methods and techniques to solve the issues related to generator stators, rotors, electric windings, insulation, controls, and instrumentation. Collaborate with other teams and industry experts to develop solutions and improvements.
Conduct electrical and mechanical testing, including RSO, PI, DLRO, ELCID, hi-pot, partial discharge, and tan-delta testing.
Set up and operate testing equipment, ensuring adherence to safety protocols.
Accurately collect test data and measurements. Analyze and interpret measurements using statistical methods and engineering tools to draw meaningful conclusions, and make data-driven recommendations.
Prepare detailed test reports and project reports, including methodology, results, and analysis. Communicate findings and recommendations to stakeholders.
Ensure project activities comply with industry standards, safety regulations, and internal quality management systems.
Develop and manage plans for assessment and maintanence of the lab’s test equipment.
Write functional specifications, project requirements, test plans, design documentation, and training documentation.
Coach and mentor other team members to support their career growth and to ensure skills retention in the lab.
Identify opportunities to enhance test methodology, equipment, and processes. Drive continuous improvement initiatives in the  test lab.
Understand and comply with all applicable Company policies and rules.
What you’ll Need To Succeed:
Technical degree with a minimum three years of experience in a generator specialist or generator field services role OR High school diploma with a minimum five years of experience in a generator specialist or generator field services role.
Minimum of three years of experience in power plant maintenance, turbine generator maintenance, and/or generator drive maintenance in an industrial, utility or oil and gas setting.
Excellent understanding of electrical generators, including generator design, maintenance methodologies, controls, protection, and instrumentation.
3+ years of experience in electrical testing and assessments of generator stators, rotors, windings, and insulation.
Proficient with relevant lab instrumentation, scopes, DMMs, high-voltage, and high-current measurements.
Adherence to safety protocols and commitment to maintaining a safe work environment.
Meticulous approach to data collection and documentation to ensure accuracy and precision.
Ability to coach and mentor other team members, setting work and testing standards for others in the department.
Ability to work in a team environment, contribute ideas, and support team goals.
Preferred
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or a related field.
Minimum of three years of experience in turbine generator maintenance, or power plant equipment maintenance, installation, and/or commissioning.

Join Our Team as a Mechanical Engineer III!
Are you passionate about  Mechanical Engineering ? S&C Electric Company is seeking a dynamic individual to coordinate our  engineering  function. As a  Mechanical Engineer III , you’ll be crucial in ensuring smooth operations and supporting our diverse team.  The Mechanical Engineer III demonstrates strong technical expertise in mechanical and electromechanical systems. They lead complex problem-solving efforts, mentor junior engineers, and contribute to the full product development life cycle.
Key Responsibilities:
Product Support: Provide support and guidance across the entire product development cycle, from concept to validation and release. Ensure designs meet performance, reliability, and manufacturing standards. Manage root cause analysis, troubleshoot production problems, and assist in RMA analysis.
Simulation & Technical Analysis: Apply mechanical knowledge to design and analyze components and systems. Conduct stress and strain evaluations, tolerance analysis, and validation testing. Use engineering tools and simulations to solve complex design challenges.
Design & Documentation: Create mechanical designs from concept to production using CAD tools. Ensure accuracy and completeness of engineering schematics and documentation. Proficient knowledge of GD&T principles and their application to engineering drawings.

New Product Design: Oversee the creation of new products by developing mechanical concepts and refining designs for performance, cost, and manufacturability. Assist in prototyping development, design validation, and participate in design reviews with cross-functional teams.
Continuous Improvement: Drive Mechanical Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) for electromechanical subsystems. The lead will identify potential failure modes, assess risks, and recommend design or process improvements to mitigate oversight.

Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field.

Good skills in effective problem-solving and able to communicate across some levels of the organization related to concepts of supply-chain, production, and electronics.

Good interpersonal skills to establish meaningful relationships built on mutual trust and respect, and foster collaborative working relationships amongst a diverse audience.

Join Our Team as a Mold Machine Operator!
In this job you will mold a variety of epoxy parts and may perform other tasks such as sandblasting and painting of molded epoxy parts. You will work in a production environment, engage in continuous productive activity, and must meet requirements within time constraints driven by machine cycles ranging from 7 minutes to 22 minutes. Tasks require a high degree of eye-hand coordination, manual dexterity, and the use of both hands and arms on a repetitive basis for a full range of motion. You will frequently use hand and power tools such as knives, scrapers, engravers and air-impact tools. As a Mold Machine Operator, you’ll be crucial in ensuring smooth operations and supporting our diverse team.
Key Responsibilities:
Operate injection molding machine, ensuring the smooth and efficient production of simple polymer components.
Review job orders and simple blueprints to understand molding requirements.
Set up molds, adjust parameters, and monitor production, maintaining optimal operating conditions for the machinery.
Cycle molding machine and monitor its progress while performing secondary operations such as deflashing, inspection, visual and mechanical application of lubricating grease, and packaging of finished product.
Inspect finished products for defects, following quality assurance guidelines and escalating quality issues when needed.
Use hand tools like files, hammer, scrapper, air nozzle to blow off excess and clean molds, maintaining cleanliness and functionality of equipment.
Apply silicone mold release with a brush to ensure things don’t stick, facilitating efficient production processes.
Perform sandblasting operations as required.
Document completed jobs, ensuring accuracy and prompt reporting of issues.
Meet department targets and consistently adhere to quality and safety standards.
Understand and comply with all applicable Company policies and rules.
Work with departmental mentors to gain and apply feedback in pursuit of improved work quality.
Maintain regular and punctual attendance.
Attend in-person or virtual meetings as requested or required.
Communicate effectively and respectfully with others.
Other responsibilities as assigned.
What you’ll Need To Succeed:
1+ year of machine operation experience in a production environment.
High School/GED diploma required.
Ability to use hand tools and precision measuring instruments such as scales and calipers.
Basic knowledge of machine controls and programs.
Ability to read blueprints.
Ability to work independently and meet requirements of assigned materials requests.
Good communication skills (written and verbal) with the ability to articulate information efficiently and effectively to team members in a variety of production support departments. Able to escalate and explain issues to team leads and supervisors as needed.
Basic computer skills with the ability to review and respond to requests via internal applications.
Basic math skills with the ability to calculate quantities, weights, and measurements.
Good interpersonal and organizational skills with the ability to understand and complete requests given by team member inside and outside of the department.
Good critical thinking skills with the ability to solve problems and understand efforts to improve processes.
Good attention to detail with the ability to complete precise tasks and follow instructions accurately.
Ability and willingness to follow Health Safety & Environment procedures accurately, reporting concerns promptly to the safety action team .

Join Our Team as a Project Coordinator, Tool Room!
The Project Coordinator supports Tool Room operations by coordinating tooling projects, administrative workflows, purchasing activities, inventory processes, and departmental reporting within a manufacturing environment. This role manages tooling requests, job documentation, project tracking, supplier coordination, and systems data to ensure work is accurately prioritized, materials are available, records are maintained, and projects progress efficiently from request through completion.
Working closely with Tool Makers, Supervisors, Engineering, Production, Accounting, Sourcing, suppliers, and other stakeholders, the Project Coordinator facilitates communication, monitors project status, maintains operational data and performance metrics, and supports continuous improvement efforts that enhance Tool Room efficiency, organization, and operational readiness.
Key Responsibilities:
Tooling Request & Job Administration:  Process, track, and close tooling requests, C.I. tickets, and capital and non-capital job orders, maintaining accurate documentation, approvals, routings, purchase order references, project hours, and closeout records.
Project Planning, Tracking & Coordination:  Develop and maintain project tracking sheets, milestone schedules, priorities, and status information for Tool Room work; monitor open actions, lead times, costs and risks, and escalate delays or constraints that may affect delivery.
Cross-Functional Coordination:  Serve as an administrative link among Tool Room leadership, team members, Tool and PPD Design, requesters, Accounting, Receiving, Global Sourcing, C.I. teams, and other stakeholders to move work from request through completion and pickup.
Purchasing & Supplier Coordination:  Coordinate purchasing activities by obtaining quotes and placing orders for materials, tooling, stock items, heat treatment, and services; maintain supplier acknowledgements and shipping information; initiate returns and new-supplier setup; and resolve order or invoice questions with suppliers and internal partners.
Inventory & Asset Administration: Support inventory and asset management activities by maintaining item records, locations, min/max levels, pricing, and vendor information, while assisting with replenishment, cycle counts, labeling, and organization.
Systems & Data Management:  Enter and maintain accurate Tool Room information in Oracle, Limble, MOM, 3DX, SharePoint, spreadsheets, Tool Master Records, and related systems, including job status, inventory, asset, purchasing, shipping, and project-hour data.
Performance Reporting & Operational Visibility:  Compile and distribute KPI reports, including MER hours, on-time delivery, department safety matrix, and AIP delivery counts; analyze workflow data and identify overdue work, data gaps, and follow-up needs.
Workflow & Process Improvement:  Maintain standard work and quick-reference guides, strengthen consistent administrative processes, and recommend improvements that reduce delays, rework, waste, and variability in Tool Room workflow.
5S & Departmental Readiness:  Lead Tool Room 5S administrative activities, including assessments, boards, cleaning and BLITZ rotations, normal condition documentation, audit records, and follow-up on departmental improvements.
On-Site Operational Support:  Provide responsive on-site support for general Tool Room questions, visitor and supplier coordination, calendars, receipts, shipping documents, and other administrative needs required for daily operations.
Compliance:  Understand and comply with applicable Company policies, rules, safety expectations, and recordkeeping requirements
What you’ll Need To Succeed:
High school diploma or equivalent.
Experience providing administrative, project, purchasing, inventory, or workflow support in a manufacturing environment.
Ability to organize and prioritize multiple tooling jobs, requests, deadlines, and follow-up actions in a fast-paced environment.
Ability to maintain accurate records, compile operational data, and prepare clear status reports and KPI updates.
Working knowledge of purchasing, inventory control, supplier communication, and enterprise resource planning concepts.

Clear written and verbal communication skills for working with shop personnel, technical teams, requesters, suppliers, and leadership.
Strong attention to detail, sound judgment, and a proactive approach to resolving documentation, material, and workflow issues.
Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across functions.

Join Our Team as a Supervisor - Assembly!

Set up and operate manual and semi-automatic (robotic) welding equipment.

Ensure welding is completed to the required standards and specifications.

Maintain welding equipment in good working condition.
Work collaboratively with team members and other departments to achieve production goals.
Record and report production data accurately and timely.
Participate in continuous improvement initiatives to enhance welding processes.
Meet department targets and consistently adhere to quality and safety standards.

Other responsibilities as assigned.

High school diploma

Familiarity with the properties and characteristics of metals used in welding.
Understanding of welding equipment maintenance and troubleshooting.
Ability to perform MIG welding techniques.
Proficient in reading and interpreting blueprints, drawings, and specifications.

title: Core Enterprise Account Executive EST/CST - Remote
description:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role:
As a Core AE, you will be helping our largest and most strategic enterprise sized customers consolidate outdated technologies, digitize workflows, and unlock game-changing data insights that will transform their businesses. We are helping the companies that literally keep our lights on, put food on our tables, and build our communities to become safer, more efficient, and more sustainable. Typical sales will be $100k to $500k, and typically involve POCs, multiple stakeholders, managing trials, multi-faceted pricing negotiations, and selling to executives and CXOs.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US and requires working in EST and CST timezone.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
Your mantra is #alwaysbeprospecting: The world of operations is vast. Your customers are often out in the field and the best way to catch them is live on the phone. Samsara’s top reps do constant research to find companies and contacts to expand their pipeline.
You have innate curiosity in how businesses work: One day you’ll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.
You are a life-long learner: Samsara sales are complex. You will need to learn about businesses where you previously had little knowledge. The payoff is big but you have to be willing to put in the work.
You build genuine relationships with your customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven’t been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.
You want to be with the best: Samsara’s high-performance Sales culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.
In this role, you will:
Develop Executive-Level relationships within strategic, named accounts
Own customer engagements end-to-end, from prospecting and qualification to close
Demonstrate excellent solution-based sales process in complex sales campaigns
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices
Minimum requirements for the role:
5+ years experience in a full-cycle, closing sales role
Proven track record of consistent quota over-achievement in complex accounts and $100k+ ARR transactions
Experience handling and owning enterprise deal sizes and C-Level relationships
Willing and comfortable with strategic outbound prospecting
Excellent interpersonal skills and demonstrated ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast paced environment
Willing and comfortable traveling to meet customers on a monthly basis
An ideal candidate also has:
Experience working with line of business stakeholders (Operations, Finance, IT)
Awards for top achievement (President’s club, Winner’s circle, Top 10%)
Passion for the world of operations!
The compensation range shown spans approved pay zones for this role. Your primary work location determines the range applicable to you, which may be narrower than the full range displayed.
Annual on-target earnings (OTE) range for full-time employees for this position is below and depends on your city of residence. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.
Annual OTE Salary $222,400 — $278,000 USD Total Rewards
At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.
Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.
Flexible Working
At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.
Belonging at Samsara
At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.
Accommodations
Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email accessibleinterviewing@samsara.com or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.
Our Commitment to Authenticity
We use Tofu , a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.
Fraudulent Employment Offers
Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our  blog post here .

description:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations.
