As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About this role:
Samsara’s cloud-connected sensor platform collects observations about the world in near real-time. Samsara builds an extensive set of products, including battery-powered, wireless sensors, Linux-based IoT gateways, and Internet-connected dashcams. These devices are the building blocks Samsara uses to construct enterprise solutions for a wide range of verticals, including commercial fleet management and industrial monitoring. Through a unique integration of sensor data such as GPS, acceleration, temperature, video, and more, we enable our customers to gain greater insights into operations, identify and eliminate inefficiencies, and react to alerts all in near real-time.
As a Senior Embedded Software Engineer at Samsara, you will develop software that runs on millions of devices, deployed by our industrial and enterprise customers. You’ll tackle challenges including evaluating and selecting hardware components, bringing up new hardware platforms and sensors, building systems to gather data and detect meaningful events, and structuring recorded data to allow efficient analysis across thousands of devices while providing deep insights into individual events.
We use C for our MCU-based platforms, Golang for embedded applications on Linux-based gateways and backend services, Google protocol buffers to structure data, and various AWS technologies to process and store data. Experience with these exact technologies is not required.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-caliber team that will encourage you to do your best.
Click here to learn more about Samsara's cultural philosophy.
In this role, you will:
Shape the hardware, not just the code that runs on it. Sit in reviews with our electrical engineers and argue for the right SoC, amount of flash/RAM, and combination of sensors, then prove those choices out on prototypes that reach real customers in months, not years.
Be the first person to make a new board do anything at all. Bring up new platforms and prototypes from virgin silicon: configure I/O, get SPI, I2C, UART, BLE talking, debug system init, validate the design, and turn unproven hardware into a product.
Own the layers everything else depends on. Peripheral drivers, secure bootloaders, device firmware updates, as well as the core management layers like power and connectivity, that determine whether a device in the field quietly recovers on its own or becomes an RMA.
Chase every microamp. Design protocols and hardware management for battery-powered sensors and gateways where the gap between good firmware and great firmware is measured in years of device life.
Work with the people who ship the whole product. Partner with product, full-stack, mobile and quality engineers so the data your firmware produces arrives intact and useful as it lands in the hands of dispatchers, fleet managers, and technicians who depend on it every shift.
Raise the bar for the engineers around you. At the Senior level, you are a force multiplier for your team. Through thoughtful designs, rigorous reviews, hands-on mentorship, and sound technical judgment, you help other engineers deliver better work. You lead by example, strengthen engineering practices, and connect technical decisions to customer and business outcomes. You bring clarity to ambiguous problems, act with intellectual honesty and urgency, and deliver high-quality solutions iteratively.
What you bring
8+ years building firmware for resource-constrained systems , You have delivered reliable firmware where memory, processing power, energy and timing are all scarce, and you know how to measure, optimize and make deliberate trade-offs between them.
You have led firmware development for several new products end to end. You have taken firmware from initial concept through architecture, technical implementation, validation, and product launch, providing hands-on technical leadership throughout.
Substantial bare-metal and RTOS experience - Zephyr, FreeRTOS, or equivalent. You have made scheduling, memory and timing decisions. Mutexes and semaphores are everyday tools for you.
You have brought up new boards. First power-on of unproven hardware, at the bench with the electrical engineer who drew it up, working out whether the bug is in your code, a library, the schematic, or the part itself.
Fluency in the low-level interfaces - SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, ADC and the ability to debug the seam between hardware and software.
Real bench instincts. The usage of an oscilloscope, network analyzer, or RF spectrum analyzer, is how you form a hypothesis, not what you reach for after the print statements run out.
Senior-level scope. You have led work spanning hardware, firmware, cloud and quality from concept to shipped product. You have consistently driven consensus across teams.
Cross-layer judgment. You can trace how a decision at the driver level surfaces in a customer's experience three layers up, and you make that trade-off on purpose.
Fluency in C. You know what the compiler is doing, and you can read a linker map, a stack trace, or a corrupted heap without guessing.
You write things down. Design docs, review comments and post-mortems that other engineers can actually act on.
You ship fast without shipping badly. Comfortable iterating on customer feedback at speed, backed by automated testing and code you would be content to inherit.
You use AI smartly. It’s part of your every day work flow and multiplies your output without watering things down.
What will set you apart
BLE at depth - You understand what’s going on down the PHY and can build orchestration for the system to use in a performant and power efficient way.
Cellular IoT - LTE-M or NB-IoT modem integration, power state management, and the certification gauntlet (FCC, PTCRB, carrier approval).
Securing embedded systems end to end - secure boot, firmware signing, cryptography, and key management that survives contact with manufacturing.
OTA and device firmware update at fleet scale - A/B partitions, rollback, and the discipline of never bricking a device you cannot physically reach.
You’ve been on the factory floor - You have an understanding of the processes behind the mass production and quality assurance of electronics. You have a track record of fixing production show stoppers.

title: CV/ML Camera Test Engineer
description:
Company Background
Specter's mission is to help automate the physical world.

Today, we build video sensors with state-of-the-art AI agents that answer any question, anywhere in their environments. Our systems can automatically detect and reason about any physical activity captured on camera, from security incidents (e.g. perimeter intrusion, theft, LPR), to safety monitoring (e.g. PPE detection, injured people), to operational efficiency (e.g. material tracking, congestion monitoring). We offer both long range wireless (1km range) and wired sensor variants to suit any deployment.

Our co-founders Xerxes and Philip are passionate about empowering our partners in the fast approaching world of physical AI and robotics. We are a small, fast growing team who hail from Anduril, Tesla, Uber, and the U.S. Special Forces.


﻿﻿The Role﻿
Specter is hiring a hands-on CV/ML camera test engineer to measure how camera and optics choices affect the performance of our AI models. Working with our Optics & Camera Engineering Lead, this individual will turn experiment plans into lab and field setups, run the campaigns, push the data through our CV/ML models and report what changed and why. The work is scientific at its core: reason from first principles about optics, sensor physics and illumination, form a hypothesis, design a controlled experiment to test it, and let the data decide. This individual will collaborate with camera, CV/ML, software, hardware and field teams to put data behind every camera decision.

Responsibilities:

 - Form testable hypotheses from first principles (optics, sensor physics, radiometry and illumination), and design controlled experiments with defined variables, controls, sample sizes and success criteria before collecting data.

 - Execute experiments comparing sensors, lenses, ISP settings, IR illumination, focus and window conditions, and measure their effect on detection, recognition and LPR performance at range.

 - Build and maintain lab and outdoor test setups, including targets at known distances, controlled lighting and low-light scenes, IR illumination and chamber runs across temperature.

title: Optics & Camera Engineering Lead
description:
Company Background
Specter's mission is to help automate the physical world.

Today, we build video sensors with state-of-the-art AI agents that answer any question, anywhere in their environments. Our systems can automatically detect and reason about any physical activity captured on camera, from security incidents (e.g. perimeter intrusion, theft, LPR), to safety monitoring (e.g. PPE detection, injured people), to operational efficiency (e.g. material tracking, congestion monitoring). We offer both long range wireless (1km range) and wired sensor variants to suit any deployment.

Our co-founders Xerxes and Philip are passionate about empowering our partners in the fast approaching world of physical AI and robotics. We are a small, fast growing team who hail from Anduril, Tesla, Uber, and the U.S. Special Forces.


﻿﻿The Role﻿
Specter is hiring an Optics & Camera Engineering Lead to own camera performance across our product portfolio. This individual will own the imaging stack end to end: sensor and lens selection, optical requirements tied to CV/ML and customer outcomes, vendor and JDM programs, test campaigns and results analysis, and high volume production. This individual will collaborate with systems, software, CV/ML, electrical, mechanical, manufacturing, supply chain and test teams to deliver performant, scalable and validated camera + optical systems to the field.

The role spans the full stack. One day you'll be benchmarking sensors and lenses for a new product. Next, you'll work with our CV/ML team to translate detection, recognition and LPR performance at range into pixel density, MTF and low-light targets, or review athermal lens designs, define a slant-edge MTF test across temperature, or analyze a wiper endurance run. You'll work with systems, software, electrical, mechanical, manufacturing and supply chain, and lead technical engagements with tier-one optics and sensor suppliers.



Responsibilities:

Select sensors and lenses

 - Evaluate and select image sensors for each product, comparing low-light performance (SNR1s, QE at 850/940 nm), pixel size, resolution, frame rate, HDR, supply life and cost.

 - Select off-the-shelf lenses or specify custom designs matched to each sensor: FOV, F-number, MTF across the field, NIR correction, distortion, relative illumination and athermal behavior.

 - Evaluate and select the ISP architecture (on-sensor, companion ASIC/FPGA or SoC ISP), weighing image quality, latency, power, cost and supply, and drive ISP tuning and pipeline development for day and NIR night modes.

 - Benchmark sensor and lens candidates side by side in the lab and the field, and keep a qualified roster of sensors, lenses and IR-cut filters ready for new programs.

Connect customer value to optical requirements

 - Translate customer use cases and CV/ML performance into camera requirements using pixel-density frameworks such as IEC 62676-4 DORI.

 - Run coverage and range trade studies across sensor resolution, FOV, mounting height, pixel density, IR range, inference load, power and cost.

 - Define MTF, aperture, distortion, relative illumination, stray light and NIR focus targets, and tie them to measured model precision and recall at distance.

 - Design and run real-world field test campaigns across sites, lighting and weather, and use the resulting model and image-quality data to close the loop from camera change to quantified customer impact and drive design decisions.

Own optical and camera system design

 - Own optical performance specifications for fixed, multi-camera, panoramic and PTZ products.

 - Integrate the selected sensor, lens, IR-cut filter and mount into a camera system that meets spec across every operating condition.

 - Drive athermal design so focus and MTF hold across a wide operating range under solar loading, accounting for IR-cut filters, lens mounts, flange CTE, humidity and pressure.

 - Specify NIR illumination (LED and laser) matched to lens FOV, including frame-synced strobing, IEC 60825-1 eye safety, thermal limits and internal-reflection control.

 - Guide window, coating, heater, wiper and sun-shade design so optical performance survives years of outdoor service.

 - Use optical simulation to evaluate concepts quickly and review supplier prescriptions with confidence.

Lead vendor and JDM programs

 - Own the technical content of RFPs for camera modules and complete camera systems, and evaluate proposals on performance, cost, schedule and risk.

 - Lead technical work with optics suppliers and ODM/JDM partners on off-the-shelf selection, custom lens design, active alignment and production test.

 - Hold partners to design reviews and gate criteria from design through EVT, DVT and PVT.

Build test capability and run campaigns

 - Grow Specter's optical lab: collimators, slant-edge MTF, focus through temperature, flare and stray light, low-light SNR, IR range and FOV/distortion measurement.

 - Design and qualify optical test equipment for development, reliability and manufacturing, with documented gauge R&R.

 - Plan and run lab reliability and qualification campaigns covering thermal, humidity, condensation, solar loading, ingress, cleaning and coating endurance, and field life, then analyze results and drive decisions.

 - Define calibration (intrinsics, extrinsics, per-unit data) and production acceptance tests at our contract manufacturers.

Scale to production and grow the team

 - Take camera systems from concept to volume production with partners and CMs, driving design for manufacturability, automated focus and alignment, and yield.

 - Partner with embedded imaging engineers on sensor bring-up, driver integration and day/night switching in production.

 - Mentor engineers across camera, image quality, test and manufacturing engineering.

 - Track emerging imaging technology (large-format sensors, zoom optics, EO/IR fusion, camera arrays, computational imaging) and recommend where Specter should invest.



Qualifications:

 - 8+ years in optical, imaging or camera systems engineering, with multiple camera products shipped to volume production.

 - Fluency across the stack, from how image quality affects CV/ML and the end user down to lens design, mechanics and test.

 - Deep knowledge of image sensors, lens design and the trade-offs among resolution, FOV, F-number, MTF, aberrations, depth of focus and thermal stability.

 - Hands-on optical simulation with Zemax OpticStudio, CODE V or similar.

 - A track record specifying off-the-shelf and custom lenses with suppliers, with clear performance and cost trade-offs.

 - Athermalization experience covering both mechanical design and optical performance across temperature (focus shift, MTF drift).

 - Experience designing optical test equipment and running test campaigns, with rigorous data analysis behind decisions.

 - Experience with NIR imaging and active illumination, as well as L/M/SWIR systems.

 - Experience taking hardware through NPI with contract manufacturers or ODM/JDM partners.

 - Clear communication of optical trade-offs to software, business and customer-facing teams.



Nice to Have

 - Outdoor, automotive or security camera experience, including sealing, condensation, window cleaning and environmental qualification.

 - Active alignment and high-volume camera module manufacturing.

 - PTZ, zoom/focus optics, panoramic or multi-camera systems, and camera calibration for computer vision.

 - EO/IR (thermal) imaging.

 - GMSL/FPD-Link camera interfaces and ISP tuning.

 - Laser illumination and eye-safety certification.

 - Experience leading engineers and cross-functional technical programs.
   

Tool Proficiency

 - Zemax OpticStudio, CODE V or equivalent optical design software.

 - Imatest or equivalent image quality analysis tools.

 - Python or MATLAB for test automation and data analysis.

 - Familiarity with MCAD (SolidWorks) for opto-mechanical review.

 - Computer vision fundamentals and tools (OpenCV or similar) for image analysis, calibration and evaluating model performance.

 - Linux command line for sensor bring-up, data capture and scripting on embedded systems.

 - Hardware reliability and test methods: environmental qualification, accelerated life testing, FMEA and failure analysis.

At Starbucks, our mission is to inspire and nurture the human spirit - one person, one cup, and one neighborhood at a time. Starbucks Technologists work to achieve this mission through the use of cutting-edge technology delivered to our partners, customers, stores, roasters, and global communities.
This senior technical product manager will help shape and deliver technology that supports the operation and evolution of our coffeehouses. The role partners across business and technology teams to simplify complex workflows, modernize platforms, connect data and systems, and create intuitive experiences for partners and the teams that support our stores.
The successful candidate combines strong technical product management, platform and integration experience, and practical delivery leadership. Experience with coffeehouse or retail facilities, repair and maintenance, field service, supplier ecosystems, or other operational technology domains is a plus, but the role requires the versatility to work across a broader portfolio. Own product strategy, roadmap, priorities, and measurable outcomes for a portfolio of technology supporting coffeehouse operations and enabling capabilities.
Lead product planning and day-to-day decision making with business stakeholders, architects, engineering, UX, data, security, QA, operations, and other partner teams.
Translate complex operational workflows and user needs into clear product requirements and scalable technical solutions.
Lead product definition and delivery for custom enterprise applications and modernization initiatives, balancing business continuity, technical evolution, user experience, and adoption.
Identify opportunities to apply AI and automation to simplify work, improve decision making, and create better partner and operational experiences.
Apply AI-assisted and specification-driven development practices to improve requirement quality, accelerate delivery, strengthen traceability, and maintain alignment from business intent through implementation and validation.
Create and maintain product specifications, process and data flows, functional and technical requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, nonfunctional requirements, and release readiness criteria.
Partner with engineering and architecture on end-to-end system design, APIs, cloud services, identity and access, integrations, data models, observability, security, and technical dependencies.

Prioritize the backlog and roadmap using customer and partner value, business outcomes, operational risk, data, architecture needs, and delivery capacity.
Coordinate modernization, migration, integration transition, cutover, and change-management activities when evolving critical operational capabilities.
Define product performance, adoption, reliability, and effectiveness measures and use insights to drive continuous improvement.
Identify and resolve delivery blockers, escalate risks early, and coordinate mitigation across business and technology teams.
Build strong relationships and communicate clearly with senior business and technology stakeholders and external partners.
Coach and mentor team members on technical product management, product discovery, specification quality, delivery practices, and outcome-based planning.

Demonstrated technical acumen across end-to-end application architecture, APIs, integrations, cloud platforms, data flows, security, testing, and production operations.
Demonstrated ability to use analytics, operational insights, and product measures to inform prioritization and product decisions.
Experience leading cross-functional delivery, managing technical dependencies, resolving ambiguity, and influencing outcomes without direct authority.
Experience with agile product development practices and modern product discovery, delivery, and lifecycle-management tools.

Experience with technology supporting coffeehouse, retail, restaurant, or other distributed physical operations.
Experience with facilities, repair and maintenance, field service, work order management, asset management, supplier/service-provider workflows, or adjacent operational domains.

structured specifications that support engineering, testing, and traceability.

Join a team that values clear thinking, quantitative rigor, and customer obsession. At Bridge you’ll own meaningful customer outcomes, operate with autonomy, and have the opportunity to shape how we scale revenue across high-potential accounts.

Scripts — Secure, isolated TypeScript runtime allowing merchants and developers to customize Stripe product behavior (e.g., discount calculations, invoice logic, proration).
Custom Objects — User-defined data models (e.g., Shipments, Locations, Warranties, Entitlements) with first-class APIs, SDKs, and Dashboard experiences.
Workflows — A programmable orchestration layer (graduating to GA at Sessions) enabling no-code and pro-code business logic across Stripe, including custom actions, delays, smart retries, and 3P integrations.
These primitives are deeply interdependent, involve 10+ cross-functional teams and culminate in a flagship product launch.

title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer, ML Training Performance

If you want to learn more about our ML Infrastructure, here is one of our past talks at re:Invent. In this role, you will:

  • Own the technical strategy and multi-quarter roadmap for RL framework and RL performance optimization for driving foundation models.
  • Drive profiling and root-cause analysis of throughput bottlenecks across the compute, compiler, framework, and cluster-networking stack.
  • Partner with ML researchers, data engineers, and hardware engineers to define requirements and make architectural decisions for large-scale training infrastructure.
  • Build custom kernels and benchmarks that track and validate performance gains across the stack.
  • Mentor engineers and raise the team’s technical bar through design reviews and best practices.
Qualifications
Note: You do not have to meet all the requirements below to be considered for this position:
  • 7+ years of total experience, including 4+ years on large-scale model training platforms, with a record of leading projects end to end.
  • Deep experience with distributed training frameworks (Megatron-LM, TorchTitan) and efficiently utilizing GPU/accelerator clusters at scale.
  • Experience with RL frameworks (Verl/MILES) and algorithms (GRPO, PPO).
  • Experience with collective communication libraries (e.g., NCCL) and optimizing communication/compute overlap in multi-node training.
  • Strong command of profiling tools (NVIDIA Nsight, PyTorch Profiler, or XLA/JAX profiling) to find and resolve training bottlenecks.
  • Proficiency in Python or C++.
  • Experience with ML compilers, performance tooling, or hardware/software co-design (GPU/TPU/accelerator architectures).
  • Ability to influence across teams and communicate technical tradeoffs to both researchers and engineers.
